source.sourceQuote: On interstates, the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well in advance of the point where you must turn off.  This permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly.

lessons.plainEnglish: An interstate removes the single most dangerous thing about a two-lane road — oncoming traffic — and replaces it with speed. Everything you do has to happen earlier and be planned further ahead. Slower traffic belongs in the right-hand lane, leaving the left for passing. The numbers themselves are a map: even numbers run east-west, odd numbers run north-south, and a three-digit number tells you whether you are on a beltway around a city (even first digit) or a spur into one (odd first digit). Because entrances and exits can be far apart, a missed turn is expensive, so plan the route and check the car — gas, water, oil and tires including the spare — before you set off.
lessons.whyItMatters: The number system is genuinely useful rather than trivia: it tells a lost driver which way they are heading and whether the road they are joining goes around a city or into it. And the right-lane habit is the one that keeps the passing lane clear, which is what makes high-speed traffic flow safely.
lessons.example: You see a sign for I-470 and wonder where it goes. Three digits with an even first digit means a beltway or bypass around a city — so it will take you around the built-up area rather than through it, while the two-digit route it branches from carries on.

lessons.title: Getting On: the Ramp, the Gap and the Merge

rules.text: You enter an interstate by using an entrance ramp, paying careful attention to the signs.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You enter an interstate by using an entrance ramp.  Make sure you pay careful attention to the signs.

rules.text: An exit ramp is often next to the entrance ramp, marked with Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Often, an exit ramp will be next to the entrance ramp, marked with “Do Not Enter” and “Wrong Way” signs.

rules.text: Look for advisory speed limit signs on the ramp; they are used where the ramp curves sharply.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Look for any advisory speed limit signs on the ramp.  These are used if the ramp curves sharply.

rules.text: About halfway along the entrance ramp, start the merging steps.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: About halfway on the entrance ramp, start taking these steps:

rules.text: Check interstate traffic with quick glances over your shoulder and to the side.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Take quick glances over your shoulder and to the side.

rules.text: Find a gap in the approaching traffic and adjust your speed to meet that gap.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Adjust your speed to meet that gap.

rules.text: Do not stop on the ramp or the acceleration lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane.

rules.text: If no gap is available it may be necessary to use the shoulder beyond the acceleration lane and stop — a last resort.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop

rules.text: You cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or making room for you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

lessons.plainEnglish: Merging is a timing problem, and the handbook solves it by telling you when to start: about halfway along the entrance ramp. From that point you are checking interstate traffic with quick glances over your shoulder and to the side, signalling, picking a gap, and adjusting your speed to meet that gap — so that when the acceleration lane runs out you are already travelling at the speed of the traffic you are joining. Follow the lane and merge; do not cut sharply left across it. Never stop on the ramp or the acceleration lane, because a stopped car there is a hazard and rejoining from a standstill is far harder. If there genuinely is no gap, the shoulder beyond the acceleration lane is a last resort, not a plan.
lessons.whyItMatters: Traffic already on the interstate has the right-of-way, and the handbook adds the sentence that should change how you merge: you cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over. Merging is your problem to solve, using speed and position, not something the traffic owes you.
lessons.example: You are halfway down the ramp and the lane beside you is solid with a truck alongside. Rather than braking on the ramp, you ease off slightly, let the truck pass, pick the gap behind it, and accelerate hard into it so you arrive at highway speed. Stopping at the end of the ramp would have left you trying to reach 65 mph from a standstill with traffic bearing down.

lessons.title: Getting Off, and Where You May Not Stop

rules.text: Signal and move into the exit lane well before the exit; last-moment lane changes risk the exit or a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit.  Changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash.

rules.text: Most exits have a deceleration lane; never slow down on the interstate itself.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Most interstate exits have a special lane for you to slow down in before you reach the exit ramp.  Never slow down on the interstate.

rules.text: Wait until you are in the deceleration lane, then brake gently to the posted exit ramp limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Wait until you are in the deceleration lane, then brake gently until your speed matches the posted exit ramp limit.

rules.text: Shoulders are only for disabled vehicles, not for changing drivers or reading a map.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles.  Do not use the shoulders for changing drivers, reading a map, or other non emergency purposes.

rules.text: Do not stop in an exit gore — a driver who missed the exit may cross it and strike you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop in an exit gore (the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp).

rules.text: No parking is permitted on interstate shoulders, and parked vehicles may be towed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: No parking is permitted on the shoulders of interstates.  Parked vehicles may be towed.

rules.text: Never make a U-turn on an interstate; go to the next exit to turn around.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate.  Go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering the interstate.

rules.text: The gravel or paved median crossovers are for police and emergency vehicles only.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The gravel or paved crossovers in the medians of some highways are to be used only by police and emergency vehicles.

lessons.plainEnglish: Exiting is the mirror image of merging: you get into position early and you shed speed in the right place. Signal and move into the exit lane well before the exit, then keep your speed until you are actually in the deceleration lane and brake gently there to the posted ramp speed. Slowing on the interstate itself puts you far below the traffic behind you, which is exactly the hazard the chapter warns about. Stopping is tightly limited. Shoulders are for disabled vehicles — not for swapping drivers or checking a map — and parked vehicles may be towed. The exit gore, the triangle between the through lane and the ramp, is the worst place of all to stop, because that is the strip a driver who just missed the exit may cut across.
lessons.whyItMatters: Missing an exit tempts drivers into the two most dangerous responses available: braking hard in a live lane, or turning around. The handbook closes both doors — never slow down on the interstate, never make a U-turn, go on to the next exit. Accepting a few extra minutes is the whole lesson.
lessons.example: You realise at the last second that your exit is here. The right answer is to keep going to the next exit and come back. Braking in the through lane, swerving across the gore, or stopping on the shoulder to think are each specifically what this section rules out.

lessons.title: Speed, Weather, Breakdowns and Work Zones

rules.text: Never drive faster than the legal speed limit, and always drive at a steady speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You should never drive faster than the legal speed limit.

rules.text: Do not drive slower than 55 mph unless weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted.

rules.text: Driving much slower than other drivers creates a hazard, because others may change lanes abruptly.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you drive on interstates at a speed much slower than other  drivers, you create a hazard.

rules.text: Headlights must be on during adverse conditions, under §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code, headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions.

rules.text: In adverse conditions maintain adequate following distance and adjust speed to allow a safe stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is especially important to maintain an  adequate following distance and adjust your speed to ensure the possibility of a safe stop.

rules.text: If disabled, move well off the road, use four-way flashers, and get everyone out and away from the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle  becomes disabled, move as far off the road as possible, turn on your four-way flashers to indicate your vehicle is stopped, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road.

rules.text: Place a flare about one vehicle length behind and another about 300 feet back, on the shoulder near the through lane edge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Put a flare about one (1) vehicle length behind your vehicle and another about 300 feet back.

rules.text: In very dense fog it may be better to leave the interstate and use slower roads.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the fog is very dense, it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads to reach your destination.

rules.text: When a lane is closed, signs are posted well in advance — move over as soon as possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If a lane is closed, signs will be posted well in advance.  You should move over to the open lane as soon as possible.  Avoid waiting until the last minute to change lanes.

lessons.plainEnglish: An interstate has a floor as well as a ceiling. You never exceed the posted limit, but you also do not drop below 55 mph unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted, because a car moving far slower than the traffic around it forces other drivers into abrupt lane changes. When conditions turn, the handbook is specific: headlights on, following distance up, speed down enough that a safe stop is actually possible. In very dense fog, the best answer may be to leave the interstate entirely. If you break down, get the car as far off the road as you can, put on the four-way flashers, and get everyone out and well away from the traffic — flares go one vehicle length back and about 300 feet back. In work zones, move over as soon as you see the lane closure signs rather than running to the merge point.
lessons.whyItMatters: The minimum-speed rule surprises people, but it follows from the same logic as everything else in this chapter: on an interstate the danger comes from differences in speed, not from speed itself. And the breakdown instruction to get everyone out of the vehicle runs against most people's instinct to sit and wait inside.
lessons.example: A tire goes flat at 65 mph. You ease onto the shoulder as far right as you can, put on the four-way flashers, and everyone gets out on the passenger side and moves well away from the road up the bank. Sitting in the car on the shoulder while traffic passes at 70 mph is exactly what the handbook tells you not to do.

questions.question: Who is required to hold a West Virginia driver's license?
choices: A West Virginia resident who wants to drive a motor vehicle on public roads, unless expressly exempt
Only residents who drive for a living
Only residents who own the vehicle they drive
Anyone who drives in the state, including short-term visitors
questions.explanation: The handbook ties the requirement to living here and driving on public roads: a resident who wants to drive must hold a WV licence unless expressly exempt. It is not about ownership or occupation, and short-term visitors fall under the separate nonresident exemption rather than the licensing requirement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Who Must Be Licensed to Drive?
source.sourceQuote: If you live in West Virginia and want to drive a motor vehicle on public roads, you must have a West Virginia driver's license, unless you are expressly exempt.

questions.question: You have lived in Charleston for two years and only ever drive on a private farm road on your family's land. A friend says you still need a licence for that. What does the handbook actually tie the requirement to?
choices: Driving a motor vehicle on public roads
Owning a registered motor vehicle in West Virginia
Being over the age of 18 and living in the state
Driving any vehicle anywhere within state lines
questions.explanation: The rule is written around driving on public roads, so that is the trigger the handbook states. Do not stretch a rule past what the source says, and do not shrink it either — the moment that same driving happens on a public road, the licence requirement applies in full.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Who Must Be Licensed to Drive?
source.sourceQuote: If you live in West Virginia and want to drive a motor vehicle on public roads, you must have a West Virginia driver's license, unless you are expressly exempt.

questions.question: A nonresident with a valid licence from another state or country is exempt from the WV licence requirement under what limits?
choices: They must be at least 16 years old, and the exemption is limited to 90 days in a calendar year
They must be at least 18 years old, with no time limit
They must be at least 16 years old, and the exemption lasts one year
There is no age limit, but the exemption is limited to 30 days
questions.explanation: Two conditions travel together in this exemption: a minimum age of 16, and a cap of 90 days in a calendar year. Because the cap is per calendar year rather than per visit, a nonresident cannot reset it by leaving the state and coming back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A nonresident who is at least 16 years old and has a valid license from another state or country (limited to 90 days in a calendar year)

questions.question: Which situation does the nonresident exemption in the handbook cover?
choices: A 17-year-old from Kentucky with a valid Kentucky licence, spending two summer months in WV
A 15-year-old from Ohio with an Ohio learner's permit, visiting for a week
Someone who moved to WV last month and still holds a valid Maryland licence
A WV resident whose licence expired while they were working out of state
questions.explanation: The exemption needs a nonresident, an age of at least 16, a valid out-of-state or foreign licence, and no more than 90 days in the calendar year — the Kentucky visitor meets all four. The 15-year-old fails the age test, and the other two are residents, who must get a WV licence rather than rely on a nonresident exemption.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A nonresident who is at least 16 years old and has a valid license from another state or country (limited to 90 days in a calendar year)

questions.question: An officer stops you for a broken tail light and asks for your licence. What does the handbook say about producing it?
choices: You must provide your licence or instruction permit on demand, and failing to do so is a misdemeanor
You may provide it later at a DMV office within five days
You only have to provide it if you are being cited for a moving violation
Producing the vehicle registration instead is sufficient
questions.explanation: The duty is to provide the licence or permit on demand to a law enforcement officer, magistrate or DMV official, and the handbook classifies a violation of that requirement as a misdemeanor. Registration is a separate document and does not substitute for the licence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You are required to provide your driver's license or instruction permit upon demand to any law enforcement officer, magistrate, or official of the DMV. Violation of this requirement is a misdemeanor.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT someone the handbook says you must produce your licence to on demand?
choices: A tow truck operator removing your vehicle
A law enforcement officer
A magistrate
An official of the DMV
questions.explanation: The handbook names three: a law enforcement officer, a magistrate, and an official of the DMV. A tow operator is not on that list. Knowing the list matters because failing to produce the licence to someone who is on it is a misdemeanor.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You are required to provide your driver's license or instruction permit upon demand to any law enforcement officer, magistrate, or official of the DMV. Violation of this requirement is a misdemeanor.

questions.question: Under what school-related circumstance can a person be denied a West Virginia driver's license?
choices: They are under 18 and not enrolled in, or graduated from, an approved educational institution
They are under 21 and have failed a class in the past year
They are under 18 and attend school out of state
They are under 16 and have not completed driver's education
questions.explanation: The handbook lists being under 18 and not enrolled in, or graduated from, an approved educational institution among the grounds for denial. It is enrollment or graduation that matters, not grades, so dropping out — not struggling — is what puts the licence at risk.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Who Can Be Denied a Driver's License?
source.sourceQuote: Any person who is under the age of 18  and  not enrolled  in, or graduated from, an approved educational institution

questions.question: A 17-year-old stopped attending school in March and applies for a licence in May. What is the likely outcome under the handbook, and why?
choices: They can be denied, because a person under 18 who is not enrolled in or graduated from an approved educational institution is among those who can be refused a licence
They will be issued a licence, because school attendance is not a DMV matter
They will be issued a restricted licence valid only for travel to work
They can be denied only if they are also under 16
questions.explanation: The handbook lists this squarely among those who can be denied a licence: under 18 and not enrolled in or graduated from an approved educational institution. The age cut-off is 18, not 16, and the link between school and driving is made in the handbook itself rather than being an outside rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: What distinguishes a REAL ID/For Federal Use card from a Not For Federal Use card?
choices: It carries a gold star and meets full federal requirements for use at airports and other designated federal facilities
It is valid in every state, while the other is valid only in West Virginia
It allows the holder to drive commercial vehicles
It never expires once issued
questions.explanation: The handbook describes the REAL ID option as containing a gold star indicating that the card meets full federal requirements for use at airports and other designated federal facilities nationwide. Both cards are driver's licenses; the difference is federal acceptance as identification, not where you may drive.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: There Are TWO types Driver's Licenses & ID Cards
source.sourceQuote: You have the choice between a Not For Federal Use driver's license or ID card, or a REAL ID/For Federal Use card that contains a gold star, indicating that the card meets full federal requirements for future use at airports and other designated federal facilities and uses nationwide.

questions.question: You plan to fly domestically next year and want your licence to work as identification at the airport. Which card does the handbook point you to?
choices: The REAL ID/For Federal Use card with the gold star
The Not For Federal Use card, which is the standard licence
Either card, since both are federally accepted
A separate state identification card in addition to your licence
questions.explanation: Only the gold-star REAL ID card is described as meeting full federal requirements for airports and other designated federal facilities. The Not For Federal Use card remains a valid driver's license — it simply is not the card the handbook points to for federal identification purposes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: What does the handbook say the For Federal Use (REAL ID) card costs and how it arrives?
choices: An additional $10.00, sent to the applicant's address via USPS in 15-20 business days
An additional $25.00, issued over the counter the same day
No additional charge, sent by USPS in 15-20 business days
An additional $10.00, collected in person at a Regional Office
questions.explanation: The handbook states the card costs an additional $10.00 and is mailed to the applicant's address in 15-20 business days. Nothing in the handbook supports paying more or picking the finished card up in person — a temporary licence covers you while the real card is produced and shipped.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: Which statement about the REAL ID card is NOT supported by the handbook?
choices: It is printed and handed to you at the counter on the day you apply
It costs an additional $10.00
It is sent to the applicant's address via USPS
Delivery takes 15-20 business days
questions.explanation: The handbook says the card is sent to the applicant's address by USPS in 15-20 business days, which is the opposite of same-day counter issue. The extra $10.00 fee and the mailing time are both stated; only the counter-issue claim is invented.

questions.question: What must a first-time applicant for an instruction permit, licence or ID card provide?
choices: A Social Security number, one proof of identity, two proofs of WV residency, and the DMV-DS-23P
Two proofs of identity and one proof of WV residency
A Social Security card and a school report card
A Social Security number and one proof of WV residency
questions.explanation: The handbook lists four items for a first-time applicant: the Social Security number, one proof of identity document, two proofs of WV residency documents, and the DMV-DS-23P provided by DMV. The counts matter — identity is one document, residency is two.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Any first-time applicant for an instruction permit, driver's license, or identification card must provide their Social Security number, one (1) proof of identity document, two (2) proofs of WV residency documents, and the DMV-DS-23P provided by DMV.

questions.question: A 15-year-old arrives at DMV for a first permit with a certified birth certificate, a Social Security card and one utility bill in a parent's name. What is missing?
choices: A second proof of WV residency, plus the DMV-DS-23P form
Nothing — those three documents satisfy the requirement
A second proof of identity
A school enrollment letter, which is the only accepted residency proof
questions.explanation: First-time applicants need two proofs of WV residency, and only one has been brought. The DMV-DS-23P is also on the handbook's list of what a first-time applicant must provide, so the trip fails on two counts rather than one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Any first-time applicant for an instruction permit, driver's license, or identification card must provide their Social Security number, one (1) proof of identity document, two (2) proofs of WV residency documents, and the DMV-DS-23P provided by DMV.

questions.question: Which birth record does the handbook say is NOT acceptable as proof of identity?
choices: A hospital birth certificate
A U.S. Department of State birth certificate
A U.S. Military birth certificate
An original or certified copy of a U.S. issued birth certificate
questions.explanation: The handbook states plainly that U.S. Department of State and U.S. Military birth certificates are acceptable, while hospital birth certificates and Bureau of Census records are not. The decorative hospital certificate many families keep is exactly the document this rule excludes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: Your family has your hospital birth certificate framed at home. What does the handbook say you should bring to DMV instead?
choices: An original or certified copy of a U.S. issued birth certificate
A photocopy of the hospital certificate, signed by a parent
A notarised statement from your parents confirming your identity
A school photo identification card
questions.explanation: Hospital birth certificates are specifically listed as not acceptable, and the acceptable proof-of-identity list begins with an original or certified copy of a U.S. issued birth certificate. Notarising or photocopying an unacceptable document does not make it acceptable.

questions.question: How many proofs of West Virginia residency must you provide?
choices: Two
One
Three
None, if you present a certified birth certificate
questions.explanation: The handbook's proof-document list states you must have two proofs of West Virginia residency. This is the count people most often get wrong, because identity needs only one document while residency needs two.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: A first-time applicant brings a certified birth certificate, a Social Security card, a current WV vehicle registration card and a WV bank statement. How does that measure against the residency requirement?
choices: It satisfies it — the registration card and bank statement are two residency documents
It falls short, because only one residency document has been provided
It falls short, because a bank statement can never prove residency
It exceeds it, because only one residency document is required
questions.explanation: Two proofs of WV residency are required, and the applicant has two separate documents from the residency list. Identity and Social Security are proved by their own documents and do not count toward the residency pair.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Proof Documents Required to Obtain a Driver's License

questions.question: Which residency document problem does the handbook specifically call out?
choices: A document showing a PO Box, or a recurring document more than 90 days old
A document printed rather than handwritten
A document in a parent's name rather than the applicant's
A document issued by an out-of-state bank
questions.explanation: The handbook states that documents with a PO Box are not acceptable and that any recurring document, such as a utility bill, cannot be more than 90 days old. A PO Box does not establish a physical address, which is what residency proof is for.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: You bring two WV utility bills, both mailed to your PO Box, the newer one dated last month. Why will these not work?
choices: Documents showing a PO Box are not acceptable, regardless of how recent they are
They would work, since one is under 90 days old
Only the older one fails, because it exceeds 90 days
Utility bills are never acceptable proof of residency
questions.explanation: Age and address are two separate tests, and these bills fail the address one: a PO Box is not accepted at all. Utility bills are on the acceptable list — but only when they carry a physical WV address and are no more than 90 days old.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

questions.question: For an applicant 18 or over, which tests come first and what do they earn?
choices: The vision and knowledge tests, which earn a regular Class E instruction permit
The road skills test, which earns a Class E driver's license
The knowledge test alone, which earns a Level 2 intermediate licence
A vision test alone, which earns a temporary permit
questions.explanation: Once the application and documents are accepted you take the vision and knowledge tests, and passing both produces a regular Class E instruction permit. The road skills test comes later and is a separate step, not part of getting the permit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: When you have completed the application and presented the appropriate documents, you will be allowed to take the vision and knowledge tests.  When you pass the vision and knowledge tests, you will be issued a regular Class E instruction permit.

questions.question: Which sequence matches what the handbook describes for an adult first-time applicant?
choices: Application and documents accepted, then vision and knowledge tests, then a Class E instruction permit
Vision test, then road skills test, then documents checked
Knowledge test taken at home, then a licence issued by mail
Documents accepted, then a Class E licence issued, then the knowledge test
questions.explanation: The handbook puts document acceptance first, then the vision and knowledge tests, and only then the permit. The order is worth holding on to because each stage gates the next — nothing is tested before the paperwork clears.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: When you have completed the application and presented the appropriate documents, you will be allowed to take the vision and knowledge tests.  When you pass the vision and knowledge tests, you will be issued a regular Class E instruction permit.

questions.question: How long is a regular instruction permit valid, and what happens if it expires?
choices: Six months; if it expires you must retake both the vision and knowledge tests
One year; if it expires you may renew it at any Regional Office
Six months; if it expires you may renew it once without retesting
Two years; if it expires you must retake the road skills test
questions.explanation: The handbook gives the permit a six-month life and states that if it expires you must retest, taking both the vision and knowledge tests for another permit. There is no renewal path that skips the tests.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: permit will be valid for a period of six (6) months.  If expired, YOU MUST RETEST, taking both the vision and knowledge tests to obtain another instruction permit.

questions.question: You received a regular instruction permit in January and never scheduled a road test. In September you decide to start again. What do you face?
choices: Retaking both the vision and knowledge tests, because the permit expired after six months
Paying a late fee, after which the old permit is reinstated
Retaking only the knowledge test, since vision results do not expire
Nothing — the permit remains valid until you pass the road test
questions.explanation: Six months from January runs out in July, so by September the permit has expired. The handbook's remedy for an expired permit is retesting on both the vision and knowledge tests, not a renewal or a partial retest.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: permit will be valid for a period of six (6) months.  If expired, YOU MUST RETEST, taking both the vision and knowledge tests to obtain another instruction permit.

questions.question: If you have never held a Level 2 graduated licence or comparable, how long must you hold the instruction permit before the road skills test?
choices: At least 30 days
At least 7 days
At least 90 days
There is no minimum period
questions.explanation: The handbook sets a floor of at least 30 days holding the instruction permit before you are eligible for the road skills test. The condition attached to it matters: it applies to applicants who have never been licensed at Level 2 graduated or comparable.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: If you have never been licensed as Level 2 graduated driver's license or comparable, you must maintain the instruction permit for at least 30 days before you are eligible to take the road skills test.

questions.question: An adult applicant who has never held any graduated licence passes the knowledge test on 3 April and wants the earliest possible road test. What is the constraint?
choices: The permit must be held at least 30 days, so the road skills test cannot come before early May
There is no waiting period for applicants 18 and over
The permit must be held 6 months before any road test
The road test can be taken the same week, as long as the permit is valid
questions.explanation: The 30-day minimum applies to anyone who has never been licensed at Level 2 graduated or comparable, including adults. Counting 30 days from 3 April puts the earliest road test in early May, well inside the permit's six-month life.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: If you have never been licensed as Level 2 graduated driver's license or comparable, you must maintain the instruction permit for at least 30 days before you are eligible to take the road skills test.

questions.question: What does the handbook say about the exam room during testing?
choices: No cell phones or other electronic devices are permitted, and only the applicant taking the test may be in the room
Phones must be switched off but may be kept in a pocket
A parent may accompany an applicant under 18
Electronic devices are allowed if they are not used during the test
questions.explanation: The handbook bars cell phones, PDAs, Bluetooth and other electronic devices from the exam room and states that only the applicant taking the test is allowed in it. The rule is about presence, not use, so a silenced phone in your pocket is still a device in the room.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: No cell phones, PDA, Bluetooth devices, electronic devices, etc. will be permitted in the exam room.  Only the applicant taking the test is allowed in the exam room.

questions.question: A parent asks to sit with their 15-year-old during the knowledge test to help them stay calm. What does the handbook allow?
choices: Only the applicant taking the test is allowed in the exam room
A parent or guardian may sit in but not speak
A parent may stay for the first ten minutes
Anyone may observe as long as they do not use a phone
questions.explanation: The handbook allows only the applicant taking the test in the exam room, without exception for parents or guardians. The same passage bars electronic devices, so the room is deliberately kept free of both people and devices that could assist.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Regular Instruction Permit - Ages 18 and Over
source.sourceQuote: No cell phones, PDA, Bluetooth devices, electronic devices, etc. will be permitted in the exam room.  Only the applicant taking the test is allowed in the exam room.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Level 1 GDL instruction permit?
questions.explanation: The Level 1 GDL instruction permit requirements begin with being at least 15 years of age. Fifteen is the entry point to the graduated system; 16 is the Level 2 threshold and 17 is the Level 3 threshold, which is why these three numbers are easy to mix up.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must be at least 15 years of age.

questions.question: Which applicant meets the Level 1 GDL age requirement?
choices: A 15-year-old with parental consent
A 14-year-old who has completed driver's education
A 14-year-old with parental consent and a signed log sheet
A 13-year-old who is legally emancipated
questions.explanation: The age floor for Level 1 is 15, and nothing in the handbook lets driver's education, a log sheet or emancipation lower it. Consent is a separate requirement that sits on top of the age requirement rather than replacing it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must be at least 15 years of age.

questions.question: What consent does a Level 1 GDL instruction permit require?
choices: Written consent from a parent or legal guardian on form DMV-DS-23P
Verbal consent from a parent at the counter
Written consent from any licensed adult over 21
A notarised letter from the applicant's school
questions.explanation: The requirement is written consent from a parent or legal guardian, given on form DMV-DS-23P. The specific form matters — it is the same form the handbook lists among a first-time applicant's required documents.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must have written consent from a Parent or Legal Guardian on form DMV-DS-23P.

questions.question: A 15-year-old comes to DMV with an uncle who is willing to sign for the permit. What does the handbook require?
choices: Written consent from a parent or legal guardian on form DMV-DS-23P
Written consent from any relative over 21
Written consent from the adult who will supervise the driving
No consent, provided the applicant has a certified birth certificate
questions.explanation: Consent must come from a parent or legal guardian on form DMV-DS-23P. An uncle qualifies only if he is the legal guardian, and being the person who will supervise the driving is a different role with no signing authority of its own.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must have written consent from a Parent or Legal Guardian on form DMV-DS-23P.

questions.question: On a Level 1 GDL instruction permit, who must be in the vehicle and where?
choices: A licensed driver at least 21 years old, in the right front passenger seat
A licensed driver at least 18 years old, anywhere in the vehicle
A parent or legal guardian, in any seat
A licensed driver at least 21 years old, who may sit in the back seat
questions.explanation: The rule names both the person and the seat: a licensed driver at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat. Putting that supervisor in the back would not satisfy it, because the seat is part of the requirement, not a detail.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive with a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat.

questions.question: You hold a Level 1 permit. Your 22-year-old licensed cousin rides in the back seat and your 19-year-old licensed friend sits up front. Is this permitted?
choices: No — the licensed driver who is at least 21 must be in the right front passenger seat
Yes, because a licensed driver over 21 is in the vehicle
Yes, because someone licensed is in the front passenger seat
No, because no passengers at all are allowed at Level 1
questions.explanation: Both halves of the rule have to be satisfied at once: the supervising driver must be at least 21 and must be in the right front passenger seat. Here the 21-plus driver is in the wrong seat and the person in the right seat is too young, so neither half lines up.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive with a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat.

questions.question: Which person could lawfully supervise a Level 1 permit holder?
choices: A licensed 24-year-old seated in the right front passenger seat
A licensed 20-year-old seated in the right front passenger seat
An unlicensed 30-year-old seated in the right front passenger seat
A licensed 24-year-old seated directly behind the driver
questions.explanation: Three things must be true of the supervisor: licensed, at least 21, and in the right front passenger seat. The 20-year-old fails on age, the unlicensed adult fails on licensure, and the correctly aged driver in the back fails on position.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive with a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat.

questions.question: Between which hours may a Level 1 GDL instruction permit holder drive?
choices: 5:00 am and 10:00 pm
6:00 am and 9:00 pm
5:00 am and midnight
Sunrise and sunset
questions.explanation: The Level 1 requirements state driving only between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm. The window is fixed by the clock, not by daylight, so it does not shift with the seasons.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive between the hours of 5:00 am and 10:00 pm.

questions.question: It is 10:20 pm in June and still light out. Your licensed 30-year-old parent is in the right front seat. May you drive on your Level 1 permit?
choices: No — Level 1 driving is limited to the hours between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm
Yes, because a qualified supervising driver is present
Yes, because it is still light outside
Yes, provided you are driving directly home
questions.explanation: Supervision and hours are separate restrictions and both must be met. The window closes at 10:00 pm by the clock regardless of daylight, and the handbook lists no 'driving straight home' exception at Level 1.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive between the hours of 5:00 am and 10:00 pm.

questions.question: How many additional non-family passengers may a Level 1 permit holder carry?
choices: Two, in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver
None at all
One, in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver
Three, in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver
questions.explanation: The handbook allows two additional non-family passengers in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver. The supervisor is counted separately, so the vehicle can lawfully hold the driver, the supervisor and two others.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only have two (2) additional non family passengers in addition to the supervising, licensed adult driver.

questions.question: On your Level 1 permit, your licensed 35-year-old aunt is in the right front seat and three school friends are in the back. What is wrong?
choices: Only two additional non-family passengers are allowed besides the supervising adult
Nothing — passengers are unrestricted when a supervisor is present
The supervising adult must be a parent, not an aunt
No passengers other than the supervising adult may ride at Level 1
questions.explanation: The limit is two additional non-family passengers on top of the supervising licensed adult driver, and three friends is one too many. The supervisor's relationship to you is not restricted — what matters is that they are licensed and at least 21.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only have two (2) additional non family passengers in addition to the supervising, licensed adult driver.

questions.question: What does zero tolerance mean for a Level 1 permit holder?
choices: No measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle
A blood alcohol level below 0.08
A blood alcohol level below 0.02
No alcohol consumed within eight hours of driving
questions.explanation: The handbook spells zero tolerance out as not having any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle. It is not a lowered numeric limit and not a waiting period — measurable is the threshold.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: ZERO Tolerance: You may not have any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about alcohol and a Level 1 permit holder is NOT correct?
choices: A small amount is acceptable as long as the driver is under the adult limit of 0.08
Any measurable amount of alcohol while driving violates the zero tolerance rule
The restriction applies while operating a motor vehicle
Zero tolerance is listed among the Level 1 GDL requirements
questions.explanation: Zero tolerance replaces the adult threshold rather than sitting beneath it, so 'under 0.08' is no defence for a permit holder — any measurable amount is a violation. The other three statements track what the Level 1 requirements say.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: ZERO Tolerance: You may not have any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle.

questions.question: What duty does a Level 1 permit holder have regarding safety belts?
choices: To require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law
To wear a belt themselves, with passengers responsible for their own
To require belts only for passengers under 18
To require belts only for front-seat passengers
questions.explanation: The requirement is written as a duty owed for everyone in the vehicle: you must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law. It is not limited by age or by seating position, and it makes the permit holder responsible for other people's belts as well as their own.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law.

questions.question: Two friends get in the back of your car on your Level 1 permit and do not buckle up. Under the Level 1 requirements, whose problem is that?
choices: Yours — the permit holder must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law
Theirs alone, since each passenger is responsible for their own belt
The supervising adult's, since they are the licensed driver
No one's, because back-seat passengers are exempt
questions.explanation: The Level 1 requirement places the duty on the permit holder to require all occupants to comply with the safety belt law. Sitting in the back does not remove a passenger from 'all occupants', and the supervising adult's presence does not transfer the duty away from you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law.

questions.question: When may a Level 1 permit holder use a wireless communication device while driving?
choices: Only to contact a 9-1-1 system
Any time, provided it is hands-free
Only when the supervising adult is holding the phone
Only when the vehicle is moving under 25 mph
questions.explanation: For a Level 1 permit holder the handbook allows no wireless device use while driving except for contacting a 9-1-1 system. Note this is stricter than the general hands-free rule for licensed adults — at Level 1 even hands-free use is not carved out.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle, unless the use of the wireless communication device is for contacting a 9-1-1 system

questions.question: You are driving on your Level 1 permit and want to take a hands-free call from your mother through the car's speakers. What does the handbook permit?
choices: Not this — device use is barred unless it is for contacting a 9-1-1 system
This is fine, because hands-free use is always allowed
This is fine, because a parent is calling
This is fine, because the supervising adult can answer for you
questions.explanation: The Level 1 exception is narrow and specific: contacting a 9-1-1 system. Hands-free operation is what makes device use lawful for licensed adult drivers, but the graduated-driver rule does not repeat that carve-out.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle, unless the use of the wireless communication device is for contacting a 9-1-1 system

questions.question: When does a Level 1 GDL instruction permit expire?
choices: On the applicant's 18th birthday
Six months after it is issued
On the applicant's 17th birthday
Two years after it is issued
questions.explanation: A Level 1 permit is issued up to the applicant's 18th birthday and expires on that birthday, with a 30-day grace period allowed to complete the road skills examination. Its life is tied to your age rather than to a fixed number of months from issue.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 1 GDL instruction permit will be issued up to the applicant's 18th birthday, and will expire on the 18th birthday.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the life of a Level 1 GDL instruction permit?
choices: It runs up to the 18th birthday and expires then, with a 30-day grace period for the road skills examination
It runs for six months and can be renewed twice
It runs until the holder passes the road skills test, with no expiry
It runs to the 21st birthday
questions.explanation: The handbook ties expiry to the 18th birthday and adds a 30-day grace period beyond it so there is time to complete the Road Skills Examination. It is also nonrenewable, so the grace period is the only extension the handbook describes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 1 GDL instruction permit will be issued up to the applicant's 18th birthday, and will expire on the 18th birthday.

questions.question: Who is eligible for a Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license?
choices: Someone between 16 and 18 who has completed all the Level 1 GDL requirements
Anyone 15 or older who has held a permit for 30 days
Anyone under 18 who has passed a road skills test
Someone between 17 and 21 who has completed driver's education
questions.explanation: The handbook sets the gate at being between 16 and 18 and having completed all the Level 1 requirements. Age alone is not enough, and completing Level 1 requirements without reaching 16 is not enough either.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you are between the ages of 16 and 18 and have completed all the requirements of the Level 1 GDL instruction permit, you will be eligible for a Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license.

questions.question: A 15-year-old has held a Level 1 permit for eight conviction-free months and completed a 50-hour driving log. Can they move to Level 2?
choices: No — Level 2 eligibility starts at 16
Yes, because the time and log requirements are met
Yes, but only with additional parental consent
No, because 12 conviction-free months are required
questions.explanation: Time served and the driving log are necessary but not sufficient: the handbook opens Level 2 to applicants between 16 and 18. The 12-month conviction-free requirement belongs to the step from Level 2 to Level 3, not this one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you are between the ages of 16 and 18 and have completed all the requirements of the Level 1 GDL instruction permit, you will be eligible for a Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license.

questions.question: How much conviction-free driving at Level 1 is required before applying for Level 2?
choices: A minimum of 180 consecutive days immediately preceding the application
A minimum of 90 consecutive days
A minimum of 12 months
A minimum of 30 days
questions.explanation: The handbook requires a minimum of 180 consecutive days of conviction-free driving at Level 1 immediately preceding the Level 2 application. Both 'consecutive' and 'immediately preceding' matter, because a conviction breaks the run and it has to be rebuilt.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a minimum of 180 consecutive days of conviction-free driving at Level 1 GDL immediately preceding the date of your Level 2 application

questions.question: Which of these would satisfy the Level 1 time requirement for a Level 2 application?
choices: 180 consecutive conviction-free days ending on the day of the application
200 days on a permit that included a conviction 60 days ago
180 days spread over two separate permits
90 conviction-free days plus a driver's education course
questions.explanation: The requirement is 180 consecutive conviction-free days immediately before the application, so a conviction 60 days ago restarts the count and leaves the applicant well short. Driver's education substitutes for the 50-hour log, not for the conviction-free period.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a minimum of 180 consecutive days of conviction-free driving at Level 1 GDL immediately preceding the date of your Level 2 application

questions.question: What behind-the-wheel evidence does Level 2 require?
choices: A certified log of at least 50 hours including at least 10 at night, or an approved driver's education course
A certified log of at least 30 hours including 5 at night
A certified log of at least 50 hours, all of which may be in daylight
An instructor's letter confirming 20 hours of practice
questions.explanation: The handbook asks for a parent or legal guardian certified log sheet of at least 50 hours behind the wheel including at least 10 hours at night, and offers an approved driver's education course as the alternative. The night hours are part of the 50, not extra.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a parent or legal guardian certification (log sheet) of  a minimum  of 50 hours behind the wheel, including the  minimum of 10 hours at night or complete a driver's education course approved by the West Virginia Department of Education

questions.question: A Level 1 permit holder has logged 52 hours of driving, all of it after school before dark. What is the problem?
choices: At least 10 of the 50 hours must be at night
Nothing — 52 hours exceeds the 50-hour requirement
The log must show 60 hours if no driver's education course was taken
Only hours supervised by a certified instructor count
questions.explanation: Hitting the hour total is not enough because the handbook specifies at least 10 of those hours at night. The alternative route is completing an approved driver's education course, which replaces the log requirement entirely.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a parent or legal guardian certification (log sheet) of  a minimum  of 50 hours behind the wheel, including the  minimum of 10 hours at night or complete a driver's education course approved by the West Virginia Department of Education

questions.question: Between which hours must a Level 2 holder have a supervising licensed adult aged 21 or older?
choices: 10:00 pm and 5:00 am
9:00 pm and 6:00 am
Midnight and 5:00 am
Sunset and sunrise
questions.explanation: Level 2 allows unsupervised driving between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm, which means the supervised window is 10:00 pm to 5:00 am. The supervisor must be a licensed adult aged 21 or older — the same standard as at Level 1.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license must drive with a supervising, licensed adult driver who is age 21 or older between the hours of 10:00 pm and 5:00 am.

questions.question: It is 11:30 pm and a Level 2 holder is driving home from a friend's house alone. How does the handbook treat this?
choices: It breaks the rule, because between 10:00 pm and 5:00 am a supervising licensed adult 21 or older is required
It is allowed, because a Level 2 holder may drive alone at any hour
It is allowed, because driving home is always an exception
It is allowed if the driver is within a few miles of home
questions.explanation: Unsupervised Level 2 driving stops at 10:00 pm. The handbook does list four exceptions to the night rule, but visiting a friend is not among them — they are lawful employment, school-sanctioned activities, religious activities, and emergencies to prevent injury or death.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license must drive with a supervising, licensed adult driver who is age 21 or older between the hours of 10:00 pm and 5:00 am.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the handbook's exceptions to the Level 2 night-driving rule?
choices: Going to, taking part in, or returning from lawful employment
Driving a family member's vehicle rather than your own
Driving on roads posted at 35 mph or less
Driving with another Level 2 holder in the passenger seat
questions.explanation: The four exceptions are lawful employment, a school-sanctioned activity, a religious activity, and an emergency to prevent bodily injury or death. Each covers going to, participating in, or returning from the activity, so the drive home from a shift is included.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The exceptions to this rule are when the licensee is participating in, going to, or returning from: (1) lawful employment; (2) a school-sanctioned activity; (3) a religious activity; or (4) an emergency situation that requires the licensee to prevent bodily injury or the death of another.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an exception to the Level 2 night-driving restriction?
choices: Driving friends home after a party
Returning from a school-sanctioned activity
Driving to a religious activity
Driving in an emergency to prevent bodily injury or the death of another
questions.explanation: The handbook's four exceptions are lawful employment, school-sanctioned activities, religious activities and emergencies to prevent injury or death. A social occasion is not on the list, and adding passengers does not make the drive lawful.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The exceptions to this rule are when the licensee is participating in, going to, or returning from: (1) lawful employment; (2) a school-sanctioned activity; (3) a religious activity; or (4) an emergency situation that requires the licensee to prevent bodily injury or the death of another.

questions.question: A Level 2 holder finishes a shift at a restaurant at 11:15 pm and drives straight home alone. How does the handbook treat that drive?
choices: It falls within the lawful employment exception to the night-driving rule
It breaks the rule, because the exception covers only the drive to work
It breaks the rule, because all night driving requires a supervising adult
It is allowed only if the employer signs a letter
questions.explanation: The exception is written to cover going to, participating in, and returning from lawful employment, so the drive home after a shift is included. That wording is the reason a work trip is treated differently from a social one at the same hour.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The exceptions to this rule are when the licensee is participating in, going to, or returning from: (1) lawful employment; (2) a school-sanctioned activity; (3) a religious activity; or (4) an emergency situation that requires the licensee to prevent bodily injury or the death of another.

questions.question: During the first six months at Level 2, which passengers are barred?
choices: Any non-family member under the age of 20
Any passenger under the age of 18
All passengers other than a parent or guardian
Any non-family member under the age of 16
questions.explanation: For the first six months a Level 2 holder may not drive with any non-family member under the age of 20 as a passenger. The test is the passenger's age and whether they are family — not your own age, and not how many of them there are.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license holder may not operate a motor vehicle during their first six months with any non-family members under the age of 20 as a passenger

questions.question: During the second six months at Level 2, how many non-family passengers under 20 are allowed?
choices: One
None
Two
Any number, once the first six months have passed
questions.explanation: The limit relaxes rather than disappears: no more than one non-family member under the age of 20 during the second six months. The restriction only ends when the driver moves beyond Level 2.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: may not operate a motor vehicle with more than one (1) non-family member under the age of 20 as a passenger during the second six (6) months.

questions.question: You have held a Level 2 licence for eight months. Your 16-year-old brother and your 17-year-old neighbour both want a ride at 4:00 pm. What does the handbook allow?
choices: Both may ride — your brother is family, and the neighbour is your one permitted non-family passenger under 20
Neither may ride until you reach Level 3
Only your brother may ride, because no non-family passengers are allowed at Level 2
Both may ride, because the passenger restriction ends after six months
questions.explanation: Family members are outside the count, so your brother does not use up the allowance. In the second six months you may carry one non-family member under 20, and the neighbour fills exactly that slot. The hour is fine because 4:00 pm sits inside the 5:00 am to 10:00 pm unsupervised window.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: may not operate a motor vehicle with more than one (1) non-family member under the age of 20 as a passenger during the second six (6) months.

questions.question: Three months into Level 2, a driver gives a 19-year-old teammate a lift to practice. Why is that a problem?
choices: In the first six months no non-family member under 20 may ride as a passenger
It is not a problem, because the teammate is over 18
It is a problem only if more than one teammate rides along
It is a problem only after 10:00 pm
questions.explanation: The first-six-months rule bars any non-family passenger under the age of 20, and a 19-year-old is under 20. The one-passenger allowance does not begin until the second six months, and the time of day is a separate restriction that does not soften this one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license holder may not operate a motor vehicle during their first six months with any non-family members under the age of 20 as a passenger

questions.question: Which Level 1 restrictions continue to apply at Level 2?
choices: No measurable alcohol, and the duty to require all occupants to follow the seat belt law
The 10:00 pm curfew with no exceptions, and the two-passenger limit
Driving only with a licensed adult 21 or older at all times
Neither — Level 2 removes all Level 1 restrictions
questions.explanation: The handbook says that as with Level 1 permit drivers, a Level 2 holder may not drive with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require all occupants to follow the seat belt law. Level 2 loosens supervision and passengers, but not alcohol or belts.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license may not operate a motor vehicle with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require all occupants to follow the seat belt law.

questions.question: A 17-year-old Level 2 holder has one drink at a family dinner and drives home at 8:00 pm. How does the handbook treat this?
choices: It violates the rule against operating with any measurable alcohol in the system
It is allowed, because the driver is under the 0.08 adult limit
It is allowed, because a family member served the drink
It is allowed, because the driving happened before 10:00 pm
questions.explanation: The Level 2 standard is any measurable alcohol, not a number below the adult threshold. Where the alcohol came from and what time it is do not enter into it — the hours restriction is a separate rule that this driver happened to satisfy.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license may not operate a motor vehicle with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require all occupants to follow the seat belt law.

questions.question: What happens if a driver under 18 surrenders a Level 2 intermediate licence for any reason?
choices: They must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit
They may reapply for Level 2 after 30 days
They keep their place and reapply for Level 2 immediately
They move directly to a Level 3 GDL at 18
questions.explanation: The handbook states that surrendering a Level 2 licence for any reason while under 18 means starting over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit. 'For any reason' is broad — it is not limited to surrenders connected with a violation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you surrender your Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license for any reason and are under the age of 18, you must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

questions.question: Which statement about surrendering a Level 2 licence is NOT correct?
choices: The driver may resume at Level 2 as soon as they reapply
A driver under 18 must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit
The rule applies when the licence is surrendered for any reason
Starting over means meeting the Level 1 requirements again
questions.explanation: Starting over is exactly what the handbook requires — a Level 1 instruction permit again, not a fresh Level 2. The rule is triggered by surrender for any reason while the driver is under 18.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you surrender your Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license for any reason and are under the age of 18, you must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

questions.question: How does a conviction affect the six-month conviction-free period at Level 1?
choices: The six-month window starts over from the date of the conviction
The window pauses and resumes once any fine is paid
The window is shortened by 30 days as a penalty
