The window is unaffected unless there are two convictions
questions.explanation: The handbook says that with each conviction the six-month window starts over from the date of the conviction. It resets rather than pausing, which means a conviction late in the period costs you the whole period, not a few days.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You must be conviction-free for 6 months in order to graduate to a Level 2 Intermediate driver's license.  With each conviction the 6-month window starts over from the date of the conviction.

questions.question: A Level 1 permit holder is five months into their conviction-free period when they are convicted of a violation. How much longer must they wait for Level 2?
choices: A further six months, counted from the date of the conviction
One more month, completing the original six
Three more months, as a half-period penalty
No extra time, because only two convictions matter
questions.explanation: Because the window restarts from the conviction date, the five months already served are gone and a fresh six months begins. That reset is what makes a single early ticket so expensive for a graduated driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You must be conviction-free for 6 months in order to graduate to a Level 2 Intermediate driver's license.  With each conviction the 6-month window starts over from the date of the conviction.

questions.question: What happens after two convictions on a Level 1 GDL instruction permit?
choices: The permit is revoked for 90 days, after which you must re-apply and retest
The permit is suspended for 30 days and then returned automatically
The holder moves straight to a Level 2 probationary licence
A warning letter is sent but the permit stays valid
questions.explanation: Two convictions revoke the Level 1 GDL for 90 days, and when the 90 days are up the handbook requires you to re-apply and retest for the Level 1 permit. The revocation is not self-clearing — the testing has to be done again.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: Under a Level 1 GDL instruction permit, two (2) convictions will result in the revocation of your GDL for 90 days. When 90 days are up you will be required to re-apply and retest for your Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

questions.question: A Level 1 permit holder has their permit revoked after a second conviction. Ninety days later, what must happen before they can drive again on a permit?
choices: They must re-apply and retest for the Level 1 GDL instruction permit
The permit is reinstated automatically at the end of the 90 days
They must wait until their 18th birthday
They may apply directly for a Level 2 intermediate licence
questions.explanation: The handbook is explicit that when the 90 days are up you are required to re-apply and retest for the Level 1 permit. Serving the revocation period restores eligibility to apply, not the permit itself.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: Under a Level 1 GDL instruction permit, two (2) convictions will result in the revocation of your GDL for 90 days. When 90 days are up you will be required to re-apply and retest for your Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

questions.question: How long must a Level 2 holder be conviction-free before graduating to Level 3?
choices: 12 months
6 months
180 days
24 months
questions.explanation: Level 2 to Level 3 requires 12 conviction-free months, and a conviction restarts that 12-month period from the point of the conviction. The six-month and 180-day figures belong to the earlier step from Level 1 to Level 2.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You are required to be conviction-free for 12 months prior to graduating to a  Level 3 GDL.  If you receive a conviction, the 12-month conviction-free period will start over again at the point of  that conviction.

questions.question: Which pairing of level and conviction-free period is correct?
choices: Level 2 to Level 3 requires 12 conviction-free months
Level 1 to Level 2 requires 12 conviction-free months
Level 2 to Level 3 requires 6 conviction-free months
Level 1 to Level 2 requires 24 conviction-free months
questions.explanation: The handbook uses six months for the Level 1 to Level 2 step and 12 months for the Level 2 to Level 3 step. Keeping the two apart is easier if you remember that the more freedom the level grants, the longer the clean record it demands.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You are required to be conviction-free for 12 months prior to graduating to a  Level 3 GDL.  If you receive a conviction, the 12-month conviction-free period will start over again at the point of  that conviction.

questions.question: What does a second conviction for a moving violation at Level 2 require?
choices: Revocation of the driving privilege until age 18, and retesting as a first-time applicant
A 90-day suspension followed by automatic reinstatement
Enrollment in a driver improvement program only
Demotion to a Level 1 instruction permit for 30 days
questions.explanation: The handbook requires revocation of the driving privilege until you are 18 and then retesting as a first-time applicant. Enrollment in a driver improvement program is the consequence of the first conviction, not the second.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: The second conviction for a moving violation requires the revocation of your driving privilege until you are 18 and you will be required to retest as a first-time applicant.

questions.question: A 16-year-old Level 2 holder is convicted of a second moving violation. What is the practical effect?
choices: No driving privilege until 18, and then the full first-time applicant testing process
A three-month suspension, after which Level 2 resumes
Automatic demotion to Level 1 with the original permit restored
A fine only, with the licence unaffected
questions.explanation: Because revocation runs until age 18, a 16-year-old loses roughly two years of driving. On top of that the handbook requires retesting as a first-time applicant, so the driver re-enters the system at the beginning rather than where they left off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: The second conviction for a moving violation requires the revocation of your driving privilege until you are 18 and you will be required to retest as a first-time applicant.

questions.question: What effect does a cell phone or wireless device citation have on a Level 1 or Level 2 driver?
choices: The conviction-free time period must begin over again
It carries a fine but does not affect the conviction-free period
It adds 30 days to the conviction-free period
It applies only to Level 2 drivers
questions.explanation: The handbook states that a citation for cell phone or wireless device use on a Level 1 or Level 2 GDL means you must begin the conviction-free time period over — six months at Level 1, twelve at Level 2. It is treated like any other conviction for clock purposes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: If a citation is issued for the use of a cell phone or wireless communication device on a Level 1 GDL instruction permit or Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license, you must begin the conviction-free time period over

questions.question: A Level 2 driver ten months into a clean twelve months is cited for texting. What has it cost them?
choices: The twelve-month conviction-free period starts over, so Level 3 is at least a year away again
Two months, which are added to the end of the period
Nothing, because phone citations carry no points
Their licence is revoked until 18
questions.explanation: The conviction-free period begins over rather than being extended, so ten months of clean driving are wiped out. Revocation until 18 is the penalty for a second moving-violation conviction at Level 2, which is a separate and harsher consequence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: If a citation is issued for the use of a cell phone or wireless communication device on a Level 1 GDL instruction permit or Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license, you must begin the conviction-free time period over

questions.question: What must be true to be eligible for a Level 3 GDL?
choices: 12 months of conviction-free driving at Level 2, being at least 17, and completing all requirements
6 months of conviction-free driving at Level 2, and being at least 16
12 months at Level 2 and being at least 18
Passing a second road skills test at any age
questions.explanation: The handbook sets three conditions together: 12 conviction-free months at Level 2, a minimum age of 17, and successful completion of all requirements. The age floor rises by one at each stage — 15, 16, 17.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: To be eligible for a Level 3 GDL, you must have completed 12 months of conviction-free driving under a Level 2 GDL, be at least 17 years old, and have successfully completed all requirements.

questions.question: A driver turns 17 having held Level 2 for eight conviction-free months. Are they eligible for Level 3?
choices: No — 12 conviction-free months at Level 2 are required as well as being 17
Yes, because they have reached the minimum age of 17
Yes, because eight months exceeds the six-month requirement
No, because Level 3 is only available at 18
questions.explanation: Age and time are cumulative requirements, not alternatives: the driver meets the age test but is four months short on the conviction-free period. The six-month figure belongs to the Level 1 to Level 2 step and does not apply here.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: To be eligible for a Level 3 GDL, you must have completed 12 months of conviction-free driving under a Level 2 GDL, be at least 17 years old, and have successfully completed all requirements.

questions.question: How are West Virginia cards for applicants under 21 printed?
choices: Vertically — red for ages 15 to 17 and blue for ages 18 to 20
Horizontally, with a red border for anyone under 21
Vertically and blue for everyone under 21
Vertically and red for everyone under 21
questions.explanation: The handbook describes two vertical formats under 21: red for 15 to 17 and blue for 18 to 20. The colour and orientation exist so law enforcement and retailers can see the cardholder's age bracket immediately.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants 15 to 17 years old are issued a driver's license or instruction permit that is vertical and color-coded red.  Applicants 18 to 20 years old, are issued a vertical driver's license or instruction permit that is color-coded blue.

questions.question: A cashier is handed a vertical, red-coded West Virginia licence. What does that tell them about the holder's age bracket?
choices: The holder is between 15 and 17
The holder is between 18 and 20
The holder is 21 or over
The card carries a restriction code
questions.explanation: Red vertical cards are issued to applicants 15 to 17 and blue vertical cards to applicants 18 to 20, which is why the handbook says the design alerts officials and retailers to the holder's age. Applicants 21 and over get a horizontal card instead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants 15 to 17 years old are issued a driver's license or instruction permit that is vertical and color-coded red.  Applicants 18 to 20 years old, are issued a vertical driver's license or instruction permit that is color-coded blue.

questions.question: Where does a restriction appear on a West Virginia driver's license?
choices: As a number or letter code in the restrictions field on the front, explained on the back
As a full sentence printed on the front of the card
Only in the DMV's records, not on the card
As a coloured stripe along the edge of the card
questions.explanation: The handbook describes a code in the restrictions field on the front, with the explanation of that code on the back of the card. This matters because a code alone does not tell you what it means — you have to read the reverse.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The restriction will be indicated on the front of the driver's license by a number or letter code in the “restrictions” field.  The explanation of the restriction will appear on the back of the driver's license.

questions.question: You are handed a licence with a code in the restrictions field and want to know what it means. Where does the handbook say to look?
choices: On the back of the driver's license
In the DMV Online Services portal only
On the front of the card, beneath the photograph
On the vehicle registration card
questions.explanation: The explanation of a restriction appears on the back of the licence, while the code itself is in the restrictions field on the front. Driving in violation of a restriction is treated as a serious offense, so knowing how to read the code matters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The restriction will be indicated on the front of the driver's license by a number or letter code in the “restrictions” field.  The explanation of the restriction will appear on the back of the driver's license.

questions.question: Under the Drive for Five program, when do West Virginia driver's licenses expire?
choices: In a year in which the holder's age is divisible by five
Exactly five years after the date of issue, whatever the holder's age
At the end of the month in which the holder's birthday falls
In a year in which the holder's age is divisible by two
questions.explanation: Drive for Five ties expiry to age: the licence runs out in a year when your age divides by five, such as 25, 30 or 35. Once you are inside the cycle the licence is valid for five years, but the phase-in period can be three to seven years depending on your age at renewal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Under the “Drive for Five” program, all driver's  licenses will expire in a year in which your age is divisible by five (for example, age 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, etc.).

questions.question: A driver renews at 32. Under Drive for Five, in which year will the new licence expire?
choices: The year the driver turns 35
The year the driver turns 37
The year the driver turns 40
Exactly five years later, whatever their age at the time
questions.explanation: Expiry falls in a year when age is divisible by five, and the next such year after 32 is 35. This is also why an initial licence can run anywhere from three to seven years — DMV uses that first card to phase the driver into the five-year cycle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Under the “Drive for Five” program, all driver's  licenses will expire in a year in which your age is divisible by five (for example, age 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, etc.).

questions.question: How long do you have to notify the DMV of an address change, and in what form?
choices: Within 20 days, in writing
Within 30 days, by phone or in writing
Within 60 days, in writing
At your next renewal, in person
questions.explanation: The handbook requires written notice to the DMV within 20 days of the change, and states that failing to do this subjects you to a possible fine or imprisonment. Notifying the Post Office does not update your DMV record or forward DMV mail.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you change your address you are required to notify, in writing, the DMV within 20 days of the change. Failure to do this subjects you to a possible fine or imprisonment.

questions.question: You move across town and file a change of address with the Post Office. What does the handbook say about your DMV record?
choices: It is unchanged — you must still notify the DMV in writing within 20 days
The Post Office notifies the DMV automatically
It updates when your mail is first forwarded
No notice is needed for a move within the same county
questions.explanation: The handbook states that simply notifying the U.S. Post Office will not update your DMV record or allow important DMV mail to be forwarded. The written 20-day notice is separate, and missing it risks a fine or imprisonment as well as missed renewal and suspension notices.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you change your address you are required to notify, in writing, the DMV within 20 days of the change. Failure to do this subjects you to a possible fine or imprisonment.

questions.question: How long does a new resident who wants to drive have to apply for a WV driver's license?
choices: 30 days after establishing residency
90 days after establishing residency
6 months after establishing residency
Until their out-of-state licence expires
questions.explanation: The handbook gives new residents 30 days from establishing WV residency to apply. That is separate from the 90-day nonresident exemption, which applies to people who have not become residents at all.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: After establishing WV residency, new residents who want to drive in WV must apply for a WV driver's license within 30 days.

questions.question: Which driver is working under the 30-day rule rather than the 90-day nonresident exemption?
choices: Someone who has just moved to WV and taken a local address
A visitor from Ohio staying two months with relatives
An out-of-state student attending a WV university
A service member from another state stationed briefly in WV
questions.explanation: The 30-day rule is written for new residents, so establishing residency is what triggers it. The other three keep their nonresident status and fall under the exemptions instead, which is why the two time limits are easy to confuse.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: After establishing WV residency, new residents who want to drive in WV must apply for a WV driver's license within 30 days.

questions.question: What does the handbook require in order to transfer a valid out-of-state driver's license?
choices: Pass a vision screening, complete a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrender the out-of-state licence
Pass the knowledge and road skills tests again
Surrender the out-of-state licence only
Pass a vision screening only
questions.explanation: Three steps are listed: the vision screening, a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrendering the out-of-state licence before a WV licence is issued. A valid out-of-state licence spares you the knowledge and road tests, not the screening and course.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You are required to pass a vision screening, complete a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrender your out-of-state driver's license before a WV driver's license will be issued.

questions.question: Which statement about transferring a valid out-of-state licence is NOT correct?
choices: You may keep your old licence as a souvenir once the WV licence is issued
You must pass a vision screening
You must complete a brief alcohol awareness course
A transfer applicant must present the documents required of a first-time applicant
questions.explanation: The handbook requires you to surrender the out-of-state licence before a WV licence will be issued, so keeping it is not an option. The vision screening, the alcohol awareness course and the first-time applicant document list all apply to transfers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You are required to pass a vision screening, complete a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrender your out-of-state driver's license before a WV driver's license will be issued.

questions.question: A West Virginia licence that has been expired for how long requires retesting?
choices: Three years or more
One year or more
Six months or more
Five years or more
questions.explanation: The handbook sets the line at three years or more expired, including for a CDL, and requires retesting past it. The same three-year line governs whether an out-of-state licence can be transferred or must be re-earned from scratch.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Any person renewing a WV driver's license, including a CDL, that has been expired for three (3) years or more is required to retest.

questions.question: Someone returns to West Virginia with a WV licence that expired four years ago. What should they expect?
choices: To retest, because the licence has been expired three years or more
To renew over the counter with a late fee
To renew after a vision screening only
To be treated as a transfer applicant from another state
questions.explanation: Four years past expiry is beyond the three-year line, so the handbook requires retesting rather than a simple renewal. They are not a transfer applicant either — that route is for a licence issued by another state or jurisdiction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Any person renewing a WV driver's license, including a CDL, that has been expired for three (3) years or more is required to retest.

questions.question: How does the handbook describe responsibility for your actions behind the wheel?
choices: The privilege to drive carries many responsibilities, and you and only you are responsible for your actions
Responsibility is shared between the driver and the vehicle's owner
A supervising adult is responsible for a young driver's actions
Responsibility passes to the insurer once a policy is in force
questions.explanation: The chapter opens by calling driving a privilege that carries many responsibilities and states that you, and only you, are responsible for your actions. Insurance and supervision change who pays or who rides along, not who is responsible for the driving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The privilege to drive carries with it many responsibilities.  You, and only you, are responsible for your actions.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT how the handbook frames the driving privilege?
choices: Driving is a right that cannot be taken away once a licence is issued
Driving is a privilege that carries many responsibilities
You and only you are responsible for your actions
There are requirements a licence holder must be aware of to keep the privilege
questions.explanation: The handbook consistently uses the language of privilege, not right, and the whole chapter is about requirements you must meet to maintain that privilege. Calling it an untouchable right contradicts every suspension and revocation rule that follows.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The privilege to drive carries with it many responsibilities.  You, and only you, are responsible for your actions.

questions.question: What can happen if a minor's school notifies the DMV of non-attendance or excessive unexcused absences?
choices: The licence is further restricted to work, medical, educational and religious purposes until age 18 or reinstatement
The licence is revoked permanently
The DMV takes no action until the student turns 18
The student is fined but keeps a full licence
questions.explanation: A school report of non-attendance or excessive unexcused absences leads the DMV to restrict the licence to limited purposes until age 18, or until the student presents a school reinstatement authorization form and pays the reinstatement fee. It is a restriction with a route back, not a permanent loss.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences

questions.question: A 16-year-old has a restricted licence after their school reported excessive absences. What does the handbook say ends the restriction?
choices: Turning 18, or presenting a school reinstatement authorization form and paying the reinstatement fee
Passing the knowledge test again
Waiting six months with no further absences
A parent's written request to the DMV
questions.explanation: The handbook gives two exits: reaching age 18, or producing a reinstatement authorization form from the school along with the reinstatement fee. The school that reported the problem is also the body that authorises the way back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences

questions.question: When can the DMV require an existing licence holder to take a medical, written or driving examination?
choices: When the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe the driver is incompetent or otherwise not qualified
Only after a crash involving injury
Only when the driver reaches age 70
Only if the driver has 12 or more points
questions.explanation: The trigger is the Commissioner having good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified to be licensed. It is not tied to age, points or a crash, and refusing to submit to the examination is itself grounds for suspension or revocation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may be required to take a medical, written, or driving examination if the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified to be licensed.

questions.question: A driver is told to report for a re-examination and simply refuses to attend. What does the handbook say follows?
choices: Refusal is grounds for suspension or revocation of the driver's license
Nothing, because the examination is voluntary
A fine, after which the matter is closed
The licence is restricted to daylight driving only
questions.explanation: Refusal to submit to the test is expressly grounds for suspension or revocation. The examination exists because the Commissioner already has good cause to doubt the driver's qualification, so declining it resolves nothing in the driver's favour.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may be required to take a medical, written, or driving examination if the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified to be licensed.

questions.question: Which crashes must be reported, and within what time?
choices: Those causing injury or death, or property damage over $1,000 — within five days by the quickest means possible
Only crashes involving injury — within ten days
All crashes without exception — within 24 hours
Those causing property damage over $5,000 — within thirty days
questions.explanation: The handbook sets the threshold at injury, death, or property damage in excess of $1,000, and gives five days to report by the quickest means possible, oral or written. Both parts of the threshold matter: an injury triggers the duty no matter how small the damage.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Crashes resulting in injury to, or death of, any person or property damage in excess of $1,000 must be reported by the quickest means possible (oral or written) within five (5) days to the local police department if it occurs within a municipality

questions.question: A crash happens outside any municipality and causes $1,500 in damage. Who must the report go to?
choices: The county sheriff or the nearest WV State Police office
The local police department of the nearest town
The DMV in Charleston only
Your insurance company, which reports it on your behalf
questions.explanation: The handbook splits reporting by location: the local police department if the crash occurs within a municipality, otherwise the county sheriff or the nearest WV State Police office. Insurers and the DMV are not named as the recipient of the crash report.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Crashes resulting in injury to, or death of, any person or property damage in excess of $1,000 must be reported by the quickest means possible (oral or written) within five (5) days to the local police department if it occurs within a municipality

questions.question: What happens if you were uninsured on the date of a reportable crash?
choices: Your motor vehicle registration and your driving privilege will be suspended
You are fined but keep your licence and registration
Only the registration is suspended
Nothing, provided you pay for the damage yourself
questions.explanation: Being without the required WV liability insurance on the date of the crash suspends both the registration and the driving privilege. Paying the other party does not cure it, because the obligation is to have carried the coverage at the time.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of the crash, your motor vehicle registration and driving privilege will be suspended.

questions.question: Your policy lapsed two weeks before a minor collision that you report properly. Why is reporting it correctly not the end of the matter?
choices: Because being uninsured on the date of the crash suspends both your registration and your driving privilege
Because reporting late always carries a separate penalty
Because a lapsed policy only matters if someone is injured
Because the DMV cannot verify coverage retroactively
questions.explanation: Reporting satisfies the crash-reporting duty, but insurance is a separate obligation measured on the date of the crash. The handbook also notes the DMV verifies coverage electronically with insurers, so a lapse is not something a clean report conceals.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of the crash, your motor vehicle registration and driving privilege will be suspended.

questions.question: What does West Virginia law require of motorists driving on public roads?
choices: They must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance
They must carry either insurance or a cash deposit with the DMV
They must carry collision coverage on the vehicle
They must carry insurance only if the vehicle is financed
questions.explanation: The handbook states the mandate plainly: all motorists driving on the state's public roads must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance. Liability coverage is what protects other people, which is why it is the coverage the state compels.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law mandates that all motorists driving on the state's public roads must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance.

questions.question: Which driver is complying with the compulsory insurance law as the handbook states it?
choices: A driver on a public road carrying WV motor vehicle liability insurance
A driver carrying only comprehensive coverage for theft and fire
A driver who has applied for insurance but has no policy yet
A driver who owns the vehicle outright and therefore carries none
questions.explanation: The requirement is specifically West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance. Other kinds of coverage protect your own property rather than other road users, and owning the vehicle outright does not exempt anyone from the mandate.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law mandates that all motorists driving on the state's public roads must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance.

questions.question: What are the minimum liability coverage amounts provided by law?
choices: $25,000 for one death or injury, $50,000 for two, and $25,000 for property damage
$50,000 for one death or injury, $100,000 for two, and $50,000 for property damage
$10,000 for one death or injury, $20,000 for two, and $10,000 for property damage
$25,000 combined for all injuries and property damage
questions.explanation: The handbook lists three separate minimums: $25,000 for one death or injury, $50,000 for two deaths or injuries, and $25,000 for property damage. They are separate limits rather than one combined pot.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: $25,000 for one (1) death or injury | $50,000 for two (2) deaths or injuries | $25,000 for property damage

questions.question: Which statement about the minimum coverage figures is NOT correct?
choices: A single $25,000 limit covers injuries and property damage together
The minimum for one death or injury is $25,000
The minimum for two deaths or injuries is $50,000
The minimum for property damage is $25,000
questions.explanation: The handbook sets out three distinct minimums rather than one combined figure, which is why the property damage limit and the single-injury limit are both $25,000 but are not the same money. Treating them as one pot understates the coverage the law requires.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: $25,000 for one (1) death or injury | $50,000 for two (2) deaths or injuries | $25,000 for property damage

questions.question: What must be carried in your vehicle at all times?
choices: A certificate of insurance or other proof of WV liability insurance, along with a valid vehicle registration card
The original insurance policy document only
A registration card only
Nothing, provided the DMV has your insurance on file electronically
questions.explanation: The handbook pairs the two documents: proof of West Virginia liability insurance and a valid vehicle registration card, carried in the vehicle at all times. Electronic verification by DMV is an enforcement tool, not a substitute for carrying the proof.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance, which can be obtained from your insurance company, must be carried in your vehicle at all times, along with a valid vehicle registration card

questions.question: An officer investigating a crash asks for your proof of insurance, and your paper card is at home. What does the handbook accept?
choices: An image of the certificate displayed on a wireless communication device
A verbal statement of your policy number
Nothing — only the paper certificate is valid
A photograph of your registration card
questions.explanation: The handbook expressly accepts an image displayed on a wireless communication device as valid proof of insurance. You must present the certificate or other proof to any investigating officer after a crash, and at any vehicle inspection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance, which can be obtained from your insurance company, must be carried in your vehicle at all times, along with a valid vehicle registration card

questions.question: What follows a failure to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance?
choices: Suspension of both your driver's license and your vehicle registration, plus reinstatement and penalty fees
Suspension of the vehicle registration only
A written warning for a first occurrence
A fine with no effect on the licence
questions.explanation: The handbook says failure to provide proof suspends the driver's license as well as the vehicle registration, along with reinstatement and/or penalty fees. Reinstating either one requires current proof of coverage and payment of the mandatory fees.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Failure to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance will result in the suspension of your driver's license as well as your vehicle registration along with reinstatement and/or penalty fees.

questions.question: What is the penalty for filing false or fraudulent insurance information?
choices: An additional 90-day licence suspension, revocation of the registration, and possible prosecution carrying up to a $1,000 fine and a year in jail
A $100 fine and three points
A 30-day suspension with no other penalty
Cancellation of the policy by the insurer only
questions.explanation: This is the heaviest penalty in the insurance section: an additional 90-day suspension, revocation of the vehicle registration, and possible prosecution with a fine of not more than $1,000 and jail time not exceeding one year. Fabricating proof is treated far more seriously than lacking it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Filing of false or fraudulent insurance information will result in an additional 90-day suspension of your driver's license, revocation of your vehicle registration, and possible prosecution that carries a fine of not more than $1,000 and jail time not to exceed one (1) year.

questions.question: A driver whose policy lapsed shows an officer a screenshot of the cancelled card, altered to show a current date. Beyond driving uninsured, what has he exposed himself to?
choices: An additional 90-day suspension, registration revocation, and prosecution with a fine and possible jail time
Nothing further, since the underlying offense is the same
Three points on his record
A requirement to attend a defensive driving class
questions.explanation: Filing false or fraudulent insurance information is its own offense with its own penalties, stacked on top of the consequences of having no coverage. The handbook's wording — an additional 90-day suspension — shows the penalties are cumulative.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Filing of false or fraudulent insurance information will result in an additional 90-day suspension of your driver's license, revocation of your vehicle registration, and possible prosecution that carries a fine of not more than $1,000 and jail time not to exceed one (1) year.

questions.question: What does West Virginia law say about using an electronic communications device while driving?
choices: It is prohibited on a public street or highway unless the use is accomplished by hands-free equipment
It is prohibited only for drivers under 18
It is permitted if the vehicle is stopped in traffic
It is permitted for calls but not for text messages
questions.explanation: The prohibition covers any electronic communications device used while driving on a public street or highway, with hands-free equipment as the only general exception. It applies to all drivers, though graduated drivers are held to an even stricter standard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: The use of any electronic communications device while driving a motor vehicle on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished by hands-free equipment.

questions.question: How does the handbook define a hands-free electronic communication device?
choices: One with a feature or function that lets the user engage it without using either or both hands
One that is mounted on the dashboard rather than held
One that switches off automatically when the vehicle moves
One that can be used with a single hand
questions.explanation: The definition turns on engaging the device without the use of either or both hands. That rules out one-handed operation, and mounting a phone does not help if you still have to touch it to use it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: A hands-free electronic communication device has a feature or function that allows the user to engage it without the use of either or both hands.

questions.question: A driver keeps her phone in a dashboard cradle and taps the screen to change a playlist while driving. Does that meet the hands-free standard?
choices: No — hands-free means engaging the device without the use of either or both hands
Yes, because the phone is mounted rather than held
Yes, because changing music is not a communication
Yes, as long as only one hand is used
questions.explanation: The test is whether the device can be engaged without using either or both hands, so tapping a mounted screen fails it. The handbook's list of violations is also broader than conversation, covering data, games, email and text handling.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: A hands-free electronic communication device has a feature or function that allows the user to engage it without the use of either or both hands.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed by the handbook as a violation of the device law?
choices: Speaking through a voice-activated hands-free system
Composing a text message on a hand-held phone
Viewing images or data on a hand-held device
Playing a game on a hand-held device
questions.explanation: Hands-free use is the exception the law creates, so a voice-activated system is what compliance looks like. Everything else listed — composing texts, viewing images or data, playing games — appears in the handbook's own description of the offense.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Violation of this law includes using an electronic communications device that is not enabled as hands-free to engage in a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save, or retrieve an e-mail, text message, or other electronic data.

questions.question: A driver argues she was not on a call, only reading an email at a stop light. How does the handbook treat that?
choices: Reading email on a non-hands-free device is named in the law as a violation
Only calls are covered, so this is lawful
It is lawful because the vehicle was stationary at a light
It is lawful because reading is not transmitting
questions.explanation: The offense expressly includes composing, sending, reading, viewing, accessing, browsing, transmitting, saving or retrieving email, text messages or other electronic data. Nothing in the wording turns on whether the vehicle happens to be stopped in traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Violation of this law includes using an electronic communications device that is not enabled as hands-free to engage in a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save, or retrieve an e-mail, text message, or other electronic data.

questions.question: What does a first offense under the hands-free law carry?
choices: A $100 fine and zero points
A $100 fine and two points
A $200 fine and zero points
A $300 fine and three points
questions.explanation: The handbook sets a first offense at a $100 fine and zero points, and a second at $200, also with zero points. Points do not enter the picture until the third offense, which is what makes repeat offending qualitatively different.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: First offense = $100 fine and zero (0) points

questions.question: What does a third or subsequent hands-free violation carry?
choices: A $300 fine and three points
A $300 fine and zero points
A $200 fine and three points
An automatic 90-day suspension
questions.explanation: A third and subsequent offense carries a $300 fine and three points. Because points remain on the record for two years and twelve points makes a licence subject to suspension, the third offense starts moving a driver toward that threshold.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Third and subsequent offenses = $300 and three (3) points

questions.question: A driver receives a third device citation. Beyond the larger fine, what changes compared with the first two?
choices: Points are assessed for the first time — three of them
The licence is revoked immediately
The fine doubles but no points are assessed
The driver must complete a defensive driving class
questions.explanation: The first and second offenses carry zero points; the third and subsequent carry three. Those points behave like any others — they stay two years from conviction and count toward the six-point caution letter and the twelve-point suspension threshold.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Third and subsequent offenses = $300 and three (3) points

questions.question: Which use of a device is expressly not a violation of the law?
choices: Reporting a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the appropriate authorities
Calling a family member to say you will be late
Using a mapping app held in your hand
Reading a work email while stopped in traffic
questions.explanation: The handbook carves out reporting a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the appropriate authorities, and also covers officers, firefighters, EMTs, paramedics and emergency vehicle operators on duty. Ordinary convenience calls are not in the exception.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Use of an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard, or emergency to the appropriate authorities

questions.question: You come upon a tree blocking both lanes on a blind bend and pick up your phone to call it in. How does the handbook treat that?
choices: It is not a violation — reporting a serious road hazard to the authorities is expressly excepted
It is a violation unless the phone is hands-free
It is a violation because you must stop before calling
It is a violation unless you are the first driver on the scene
questions.explanation: Reporting a serious road hazard to the appropriate authorities is one of the named exceptions, alongside fires, crashes and emergencies. A graduated driver at Level 1 or Level 2 should note that their own rule is narrower still, permitting device use only for contacting a 9-1-1 system.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Use of an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard, or emergency to the appropriate authorities

questions.question: How long do points remain on a West Virginia driving record?
choices: Two years from the conviction date
One year from the conviction date
Five years from the conviction date
Until the licence is renewed
questions.explanation: Points stay for two years measured from the conviction date, not from the date of the offense or the date you paid. That two-year window is what lets separate incidents combine toward the six- and twelve-point thresholds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points remain on your driving record for two (2) years from the conviction date.

questions.question: A driver was convicted of a point-bearing violation in June 2024 and another in May 2026. How does the handbook's timing rule apply?
choices: Both sets of points are on the record together, because points last two years from conviction
Only the 2026 points count, because each conviction cancels the last
Neither counts, because they are in different years
Only the 2024 points count, because the older conviction is the more serious
questions.explanation: Points from June 2024 remain until June 2026, so a May 2026 conviction lands while they are still live and the totals add together. This overlap is exactly how drivers reach the six-point caution letter without any single serious offense.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points remain on your driving record for two (2) years from the conviction date.

questions.question: What does the DMV do when a driver reaches six points or more?
choices: Sends a letter of caution urging care and obedience to traffic laws
Suspends the licence for 30 days
Requires a defensive driving class
Orders a re-examination
questions.explanation: Six points or more triggers a letter of caution — a warning rather than a sanction. The consequence with teeth arrives at twelve points, where the licence becomes subject to suspension.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you have six (6) points or more on your record, the DMV will send you a letter of caution, urging you to be careful while driving and obedient of traffic laws.

questions.question: What happens at 12 points?
choices: The driver's license is subject to suspension
The driver receives a second letter of caution
Three points are automatically removed
The licence is permanently revoked
questions.explanation: Twelve points makes the licence subject to suspension. Revocation is reserved for the specific serious convictions the handbook lists separately, so accumulating points leads to suspension rather than permanent loss.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you accumulate 12 points on your record, your driver's license is subject to suspension.

questions.question: Which pairing of point total and consequence is correct?
choices: 12 points — the licence is subject to suspension
6 points — the licence is subject to suspension
12 points — a letter of caution is sent
3 points — the licence is subject to suspension
questions.explanation: Six points brings the letter of caution and twelve makes the licence subject to suspension. Three is the number of points an approved defensive driving class removes, which is a different use of the same figure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you accumulate 12 points on your record, your driver's license is subject to suspension.

questions.question: How can a driver have points removed from their record?
choices: By completing an approved eight-hour defensive driving class, which deducts three points once every 12 months
By completing any defensive driving class, as often as they like
By going 12 months without a conviction, which clears the record
By paying a reinstatement fee to the DMV
questions.explanation: An approved eight-hour defensive driving class deducts three points, and a motorist is only eligible for that reduction once every 12 months. It is the only point-removal route the handbook offers, apart from points simply ageing off after two years.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may have three (3) points deducted from your record by completing an approved eight (8) hour defensive driving class.  Motorists are only eligible for this point reduction once every 12 months.

questions.question: A driver enrolls in a defensive driving class the day after conviction, before the points appear on the record. What is the effect?
choices: No deduction — the class must not be taken before the points appear on the record
Three points are deducted as soon as the points post
Six points are deducted for acting promptly
The conviction is removed from the record entirely
questions.explanation: The handbook rules out a deduction for a class taken before the points appear on your record, and equally for a class the DMV has not approved. Timing and approval are both conditions, so being quick can actually cost the driver the benefit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you take a class without approval from the DMV or take the class prior to the points appearing on your record, you will not be eligible for the point deduction.

questions.question: Which of these would NOT disqualify a driver from the three-point deduction?
choices: Taking the approved class after the points have appeared on the record
Taking a class the DMV has not approved
Taking the class before the points appear on the record
Having already used the reduction six months ago
questions.explanation: Taking an approved class after the points have posted is exactly what qualifies. The other three each fall foul of a stated condition: approval, timing, or the once-every-12-months limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you take a class without approval from the DMV or take the class prior to the points appearing on your record, you will not be eligible for the point deduction.

questions.question: How are point values assigned to violations?
choices: According to the seriousness of the in-state or out-of-state moving violation
Equally, at two points for every moving violation
By the amount of the fine imposed by the court
Only for violations committed inside West Virginia
questions.explanation: Points are assigned to in-state and out-of-state moving violations depending on the seriousness of the violation, so more dangerous conduct carries more points. Out-of-state violations reach your record through the Driver License Compact.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points have been assigned to various in-state and out-of-state moving traffic violations depending on the seriousness of the violation.

questions.question: A driver assumes a ticket from a neighbouring state cannot affect their West Virginia point total. Why is that wrong?
choices: Points are assigned to out-of-state as well as in-state moving violations
Only violations resulting in a crash are recorded
Out-of-state tickets add double points
Out-of-state tickets affect insurance but never the DMV record
questions.explanation: The handbook says points have been assigned to various in-state and out-of-state moving traffic violations. West Virginia's membership of the Driver License Compact is what brings those out-of-state convictions onto the record in the first place.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points have been assigned to various in-state and out-of-state moving traffic violations depending on the seriousness of the violation.

questions.question: Which conviction involving a graduated driver requires revocation of the licence?
choices: Two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver
One moving violation conviction as a graduated driver
Any conviction for a parking violation
Three moving violation convictions as a graduated driver
questions.explanation: The mandatory revocation list includes two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver. This is the same threshold that ends the GDL road in Chapter I, stated here as a revocation the DMV must impose on notice of final conviction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Two (2) or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver

questions.question: A Level 2 driver is convicted of a second moving violation. Which part of the handbook, besides the GDL rules, applies?
choices: The mandatory revocation list, which includes two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver
The point system's six-point letter of caution provision
The compulsory insurance verification programme
The re-examination provisions for unsafe drivers
questions.explanation: The same facts appear in two places: Chapter I ends the graduated driver's privilege until 18, and Chapter II lists two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver among the convictions requiring immediate revocation. Nothing about it is discretionary once the conviction is final.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Two (2) or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver

questions.question: Which of these is on the handbook's mandatory revocation list?
choices: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury
Receiving a second parking ticket in a year
Failing to carry proof of insurance on one occasion
Accumulating six points on your record
questions.explanation: Leaving the scene of a crash resulting in death or personal injury is named on the list of convictions requiring immediate revocation. Six points brings only a caution letter, and an insurance proof failure leads to suspension rather than mandatory revocation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury

questions.question: Which statement about leaving the scene of an injury crash is NOT correct?
choices: It results in points but leaves the licence intact
It appears on the list of convictions requiring immediate revocation
The DMV must revoke on notice of final conviction
It is treated more seriously than an ordinary moving violation
questions.explanation: This offense is not handled through points at all — it sits on the mandatory revocation list, where the DMV must revoke on receiving notice of final conviction. Treating it as a points matter understates it substantially.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury

questions.question: What may follow driving while your licence is suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason?
choices: A 90-day suspension
A warning letter
Three points and a $100 fine
Immediate reinstatement once the fine is paid
questions.explanation: The handbook describes driving while suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason as a serious matter that may cause a 90-day suspension. Driving while revoked on a DUI is treated separately and far more severely, including mandatory jail time.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Driving While a Driver's License Is Revoked or Suspended
source.sourceQuote: Driving while your driver's license is suspended or revoked (non-DUI related) is a serious matter and may cause a 90-day suspension.

questions.question: A driver under a 30-day suspension drives to work and is stopped. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: A further 90-day suspension may follow, because driving while suspended is a serious matter
Nothing further, because the original suspension already covers it
The original suspension is converted to a revocation for life
The driver receives points but no additional suspension
questions.explanation: Driving while suspended is a separate offense that may cause a 90-day suspension on top of what the driver is already serving. Needing to get to work is not an exception the handbook recognises — a restricted licence, where available, is granted by DMV rather than assumed by the driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Driving While a Driver's License Is Revoked or Suspended
source.sourceQuote: Driving while your driver's license is suspended or revoked (non-DUI related) is a serious matter and may cause a 90-day suspension.

questions.question: What penalty does the handbook attach to using someone else's licence as your own?
choices: A 90-day suspension
A $100 fine and no suspension
A 30-day suspension
Permanent revocation
questions.explanation: The 90-day suspension covers a family of offenses: using another person's licence, letting someone use yours, letting someone use your identity documents to obtain a licence, and using or displaying a fictitious licence. Lending your card is penalised the same way as borrowing one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is also illegal to use someone else's license as your own, to permit someone else to use your driver's license, to permit someone to use your identity documents to obtain a license, or to use or display a fictitious license.  The penalty for these offenses is a 90-day suspension.

questions.question: A 17-year-old lends his licence to a friend who has none. Who faces the 90-day suspension?
choices: Both — permitting someone else to use your licence is itself a listed offense
Only the friend who used it
Only the owner, if the friend is caught driving
Neither, unless the friend is involved in a crash
questions.explanation: The handbook lists using someone else's licence and permitting someone else to use yours as separate offenses, each carrying a 90-day suspension. The owner is not a bystander in this arrangement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is also illegal to use someone else's license as your own, to permit someone else to use your driver's license, to permit someone to use your identity documents to obtain a license, or to use or display a fictitious license.  The penalty for these offenses is a 90-day suspension.

questions.question: What happens if you fail to appear or comply with a ticket or court order?
choices: The DMV suspends your licence until you show proof of compliance and pay all penalty fees
The court issues a warning and takes no DMV action
Points are added but the licence is unaffected
The DMV suspends the licence for a fixed 30 days
questions.explanation: Courts are required to notify the DMV of a failure to appear or comply with any ticket, court order or decision, even a non-traffic one, and the DMV suspends until you present proof of compliance and pay the fees. The suspension has no fixed end date — it ends when you resolve the underlying matter.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Failure to Comply with In-State Citations
source.sourceQuote: The DMV will suspend your driver's license until you present proof of compliance with the court action and all penalty fees are paid.

questions.question: Which statement about failing to comply with a court action is NOT correct?
choices: Only traffic tickets can lead to a DMV suspension
Municipal, magistrate and circuit courts must notify the DMV
The suspension lasts until proof of compliance is presented
All penalty fees must be paid before reinstatement
questions.explanation: The handbook says courts must notify the DMV of a failure to appear or comply with any type of ticket, court order or decision, even if it is not a traffic ticket. That is the detail drivers most often get wrong about this rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Failure to Comply with In-State Citations
source.sourceQuote: The DMV will suspend your driver's license until you present proof of compliance with the court action and all penalty fees are paid.

questions.question: What does West Virginia's membership of the Driver License Compact mean for violations committed in other states?
choices: They become part of your West Virginia driving record and points may be assessed
They remain with the state that issued them and never reach WV
They are recorded but can never carry points
They apply only if the other state is adjacent to West Virginia
questions.explanation: Under the compact, traffic violations received in other states join your West Virginia record and, if warranted, points are assessed. A conviction elsewhere that is grounds for suspension or revocation can also cost you the WV licence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia is a member of the Driver License Compact.  Traffic violations you receive in other states will become part of your West Virginia driving record and, if warranted, points will be assessed.

questions.question: A WV driver is convicted of speeding while on holiday in another compact state and assumes it stays there. What actually happens?
choices: The violation becomes part of their WV driving record and points may be assessed
Nothing, because WV only records violations committed in WV
The WV licence is automatically suspended for 30 days
The driver must surrender their WV licence to that state
questions.explanation: The compact exists precisely to stop violations being confined to the state where they happened, so the conviction joins the WV record and can draw points. If the offense is grounds for suspension or revocation, the WV licence itself may be suspended or revoked.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia is a member of the Driver License Compact.  Traffic violations you receive in other states will become part of your West Virginia driving record and, if warranted, points will be assessed.

questions.question: A driver receives a DMV notice asking for proof of coverage and ignores it. What does the handbook say follows?
choices: Suspension of the driver's license and the vehicle registration, with reinstatement and penalty fees to follow
A warning letter, with action only if a second notice is ignored
Suspension of the registration, leaving the licence untouched
Nothing, because DMV verifies coverage electronically without the driver's help
questions.explanation: The DMV may verify insurance at any point in the registration year and will require proof when it issues a notice. Failing to provide that proof suspends the licence as well as the registration, and reinstating either requires current proof of coverage plus the mandatory fees.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Failure to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance will result in the suspension of your driver's license as well as your vehicle registration along with reinstatement and/or penalty fees.

questions.question: Which statement about the hands-free law is NOT correct?
choices: It applies only while the vehicle is in motion on an interstate
It covers any electronic communications device
It applies on public streets and highways
Hands-free equipment is the general exception
questions.explanation: The law is written for driving a motor vehicle on a public street or highway, not for interstates alone, and the handbook's list of covered conduct extends well beyond a moving vehicle on a freeway. Device type, road type and the hands-free exception are all stated as described in the other three options.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: The use of any electronic communications device while driving a motor vehicle on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished by hands-free equipment.

questions.question: Which pairing of hands-free offense and penalty is correct?
choices: First offense — $100 fine and zero points
First offense — $100 fine and three points
Second offense — $300 fine and three points
First offense — $300 fine and zero points
questions.explanation: The escalation runs $100 with no points, then $200 with no points, then $300 with three points from the third offense onward. Points arrive only at the third stage, so pairing them with a first offense misstates the scheme.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: First offense = $100 fine and zero (0) points

questions.question: A driver reaches seven points and receives DMV correspondence. What is it most likely to be, and what does it mean?
choices: A letter of caution, which urges care and obedience to traffic laws but does not itself suspend anything
A suspension notice, because any total above six suspends the licence
A notice requiring an eight-hour defensive driving class
A notice of mandatory revocation
questions.explanation: Six points or more triggers a letter of caution urging the driver to be careful and obedient to traffic laws. Suspension does not become a prospect until twelve points, so the letter is a warning that there is real headroom left to lose.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you have six (6) points or more on your record, the DMV will send you a letter of caution, urging you to be careful while driving and obedient of traffic laws.

questions.question: Which statement about the defensive driving point reduction is NOT correct?
choices: A driver may use the reduction as often as they accumulate points
It removes three points
The class must be an approved eight-hour class
