A driver is eligible only once every 12 months
questions.explanation: The handbook limits the reduction to once every 12 months, so it cannot be used repeatedly to offset a run of convictions. The three-point value, the eight-hour approved class and the annual eligibility limit are all stated as given.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may have three (3) points deducted from your record by completing an approved eight (8) hour defensive driving class.  Motorists are only eligible for this point reduction once every 12 months.

questions.question: Who has to pass the vision screening?
choices: All persons, whether new applicants or renewals
New applicants only
Drivers over the age of 65 only
Applicants who do not already wear glasses
questions.explanation: The handbook applies the screening to all persons, new applicants and renewals alike. Vision can change between renewals, which is why an existing licence does not exempt anyone.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: All persons, whether new applicants or renewals, will have to pass the vision screening.

questions.question: A driver renewing a licence held for 20 years asks whether the eye test still applies. What is the answer?
choices: Yes — all persons, new applicants and renewals, must pass the vision screening
No — screening applies only to first-time applicants
Only if the current licence carries a corrective lenses restriction
Only if the driver has points on their record
questions.explanation: Renewals are named alongside new applicants in the screening requirement. Neither length of driving history nor an existing restriction changes it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: All persons, whether new applicants or renewals, will have to pass the vision screening.

questions.question: What vision standard passes the screening?
choices: 20/40 or better using both eyes, with or without conventional corrective lenses, and no serious visual defect
20/20 or better using both eyes, without corrective lenses
20/60 or better using both eyes, with corrective lenses
20/40 or better in the right eye only
questions.explanation: The standard is 20/40 or better using both eyes, reached with or without conventional corrective lenses, and with no serious visual defect. Glasses and contacts are allowed to get you there — what matters is the corrected result.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is 20/40 or better using both eyes, either with or without conventional corrective lenses, and you show no serious visual defect, you will pass the vision screening.

questions.question: Which applicant would pass the vision screening as the handbook describes it?
choices: One reading 20/35 with both eyes while wearing prescribed contact lenses, with no serious visual defect
One reading 20/50 with both eyes while wearing prescribed glasses
One reaching 20/40 only with the aid of a telescopic lens arrangement
One reading 20/40 but with a serious visual defect
questions.explanation: Reaching 20/40 or better with conventional corrective lenses passes, so 20/35 with contacts is fine. Twenty over fifty falls short, a serious visual defect fails regardless of acuity, and the handbook says special arrangements such as bi-optic or telescopic lenses may not be used to satisfy the standard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is 20/40 or better using both eyes, either with or without conventional corrective lenses, and you show no serious visual defect, you will pass the vision screening.

questions.question: What appears on the licence of someone who needs glasses to reach 20/40?
choices: A restriction code for corrective lenses
A note in the DMV file, but nothing on the card
An endorsement allowing daytime driving only
A vertical card format
questions.explanation: Needing glasses or contacts to reach 20/40 puts a corrective lenses restriction code on the licence. Restriction codes appear in the restrictions field on the front of the card and are explained on the back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you require glasses or contact lenses to have a vision level of 20/40 or better, your driver's license will show a restriction code for “corrective lenses.”

questions.question: A driver whose licence carries the corrective lenses restriction arrives for a road test without their glasses. What is the consequence?
choices: Failing to wear glasses when required is listed among the road skills test automatic failures
The test proceeds, with points deducted for the omission
The examiner may lend the applicant reading glasses
Nothing, provided the applicant can read the test route signs
questions.explanation: The handbook lists failing to wear your glasses if required among the errors that disqualify you from the road test. Away from the test it is just as serious, because driving in violation of a restriction can suspend or revoke the privilege.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you require glasses or contact lenses to have a vision level of 20/40 or better, your driver's license will show a restriction code for “corrective lenses.”

questions.question: Can an applicant with sight in only one eye pass the vision screening?
choices: Yes, if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better
No, both eyes are always required
Yes, but only with a daylight driving restriction
Yes, if the vision level with that eye is 20/60 or better
questions.explanation: The handbook says an applicant with only one eye may be passed if that eye reaches 20/40 or better. The acuity standard does not change — what changes is that it is measured in the one eye available.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you have only one (1) eye, you may be passed if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better.

questions.question: A driver who lost the sight of one eye years ago is renewing a licence and reads 20/30 with the remaining eye. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: They may be passed, because the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better
They cannot be passed, because both eyes are required
They may be passed only with a daylight driving restriction
They must first obtain a statement from the Driver's License Advisory Board
questions.explanation: The handbook allows an applicant with only one eye to be passed if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better, and 20/30 clears that. The specialist statement route exists for applicants who cannot reach 20/40, which is not this driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you have only one (1) eye, you may be passed if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better.

questions.question: What happens to an applicant whose vision is less than 20/40?
choices: They do not pass, and are advised to consult a vision specialist about reaching the 20/40 level
They are issued a licence restricted to daylight driving
They may retake the screening the same day
They are permanently barred from holding a licence
questions.explanation: Falling short means not passing the screening and being advised to see a vision specialist to determine whether the vision can be brought to 20/40. A specialist's DLAB-Form 2 statement can bring the application forward again, possibly with restrictions, so it is not a permanent bar.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is less than 20/40 or you have a serious visual defect, you will not pass the screening and will be advised to consult a vision specialist to determine if your vision can be brought to the 20/40 level.

questions.question: Which statement about failing the vision screening is NOT correct?
choices: The applicant is permanently ineligible for a West Virginia licence
The applicant will not pass the screening
The applicant is advised to consult a vision specialist
The question is whether the vision can be brought to the 20/40 level
questions.explanation: Nothing in the handbook makes a failed screening permanent — it routes the applicant to a vision specialist, whose statement on a DLAB-Form 2 may be reviewed by the Driver's License Advisory Board. The other three statements track the passage exactly.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is less than 20/40 or you have a serious visual defect, you will not pass the screening and will be advised to consult a vision specialist to determine if your vision can be brought to the 20/40 level.

questions.question: How many questions does the knowledge examination have, and where do they come from?
choices: At least 25, based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings found in the handbook
Exactly 40, drawn from West Virginia state code
At least 25, drawn from national driving standards
Exactly 20, covering signs and markings only
questions.explanation: The examination has at least 25 questions and every topic it draws on is in this handbook: basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings. That is the strongest argument for studying the handbook itself rather than anything else.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The knowledge examination has at least 25 questions based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs, and markings found in the  handbook.

questions.question: Which subject areas does the handbook say the knowledge examination covers?
choices: Basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings
Vehicle mechanics and maintenance schedules
State code citations and court procedure
Insurance products and premium calculations
questions.explanation: The five named areas are basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings. Everything the test asks about is meant to be findable in the handbook, which is why unfamiliar material is a sign you are studying the wrong source.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The knowledge examination has at least 25 questions based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs, and markings found in the  handbook.

questions.question: How many of the 25 questions must you answer correctly to pass?
questions.explanation: The pass mark is 19 out of 25, which leaves room for six wrong answers and no more. Any practice target above that, such as aiming for 22, is preparation margin rather than the official standard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must answer 19 out of the 25 questions correctly to pass the test.

questions.question: An applicant answers 25 questions and gets 6 wrong. What is the result?
choices: A pass, because 19 correct answers meets the standard
A fail, because more than five wrong answers is disqualifying
A fail, because 20 correct answers are required
A pass, but only with a retest of the missed questions
questions.explanation: Nineteen correct out of 25 is exactly the pass mark, and six wrong leaves precisely 19 right. One more error would fail the test, which is why the margin at 19 is worth treating as no margin at all.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must answer 19 out of the 25 questions correctly to pass the test.

questions.question: What happens to questions you have not answered when the time limit expires?
choices: They are considered incorrect
They are not counted either way
The test is extended until they are answered
They are marked correct if the rest of the test is passed
questions.explanation: The handbook states that any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect. A blank therefore costs the same as a wrong answer, which is why leaving questions to come back to is a risk.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: There is a time limit on the test and any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect.

questions.question: You are unsure of three questions with little time left. What does the handbook's rule suggest you do?
choices: Answer all of them before time expires, since unanswered questions count as incorrect
Leave them blank, since blanks are not counted
Ask the examiner to pause the clock while you think
Answer only the ones you are confident about
questions.explanation: Because unanswered questions are treated as incorrect, an uncertain answer can only help while a blank certainly cannot. There is nothing in the handbook allowing the clock to be paused, and DMV staff may not help explain questions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: There is a time limit on the test and any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect.

questions.question: What accommodation does the handbook describe for the reading impaired?
choices: Audio versions of the knowledge examination, administered with headphones
Unlimited time to complete the printed exam
A DMV employee who reads each question aloud
A reduced set of 15 questions
questions.explanation: Audio versions are available for the reading impaired and are administered with headphones. Headsets are limited, so the handbook warns you may have to wait if you request the audio test.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Audio versions of the knowledge examination are available for the reading impaired.  The test is administered with headphones.

questions.question: What may a DMV employee do to help an applicant during the knowledge examination?
choices: Nothing beyond what a printed-exam applicant would receive — they may not read, re-word or explain questions
Read each question aloud on request
Re-word confusing questions in simpler language
Explain the meaning of any term the applicant does not know
questions.explanation: The handbook bars DMV employees from reading the test to you, re-wording information, or providing extra help explaining questions that a printed-exam applicant would not get. The audio version exists precisely so the accommodation is standardised rather than left to staff.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Employees of the DMV are not to read the test to you, re-word the information, or provide additional help explaining questions that would not be supplied to applicants taking the printed knowledge exam.

questions.question: Which statement about the audio version of the knowledge examination is NOT correct?
choices: An examiner may explain any question the applicant finds unclear
The same information covered in the printed exam is covered in the audio version
The same rules apply to the audio version
Headsets are limited and an applicant may have to wait
questions.explanation: Explanation is exactly what the handbook rules out — employees may not read the test, re-word it or explain questions beyond what printed-exam applicants receive. Equal content, equal rules and limited headsets are all stated.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Employees of the DMV are not to read the test to you, re-word the information, or provide additional help explaining questions that would not be supplied to applicants taking the printed knowledge exam.

questions.question: An applicant who reads with difficulty asks how to take the test. What does the handbook offer?
choices: An audio version administered with headphones, covering the same information under the same rules
A shorter version with fewer questions
An oral examination conducted by a DMV employee
An exemption from the knowledge test with a doctor's letter
questions.explanation: The audio version is the accommodation the handbook provides, delivered by headphones, covering the same information and governed by the same rules. It is specifically not a staff member reading the test, which employees are forbidden to do.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Audio versions of the knowledge examination are available for the reading impaired.  The test is administered with headphones.

questions.question: What must the testing vehicle have before it can be used for the road skills test?
choices: A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance
A valid inspection sticker only
Proof of insurance and a spare tire
Nothing specific, as long as it runs
questions.explanation: A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance on the vehicle are both required before it can be used, and the examiner checks compliance with registration, inspection and equipment laws. Defects in the vehicle may constitute failure of the examination.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The testing vehicle must first be checked to make sure it complies with registration, vehicle inspection and equipment laws.  A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance on the vehicle is required before the vehicle can be used for the road skills test.

questions.question: You arrive for your road test in a car whose inspection sticker expired last month. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: The vehicle cannot be used for the road skills test, because a valid inspection sticker is required
The test proceeds with a warning to renew the inspection
The examiner may issue a temporary inspection waiver
The test proceeds if proof of insurance is produced
questions.explanation: A valid inspection sticker is a precondition for using the vehicle, standing alongside proof of insurance rather than as an alternative to it. Vehicle defects and non-compliance may constitute failure of the examination.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The testing vehicle must first be checked to make sure it complies with registration, vehicle inspection and equipment laws.  A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance on the vehicle is required before the vehicle can be used for the road skills test.

questions.question: A defect is found in your test vehicle. What does the handbook allow?
choices: The examiner may permit a minor defect to be corrected and the examination continued, but not in another vehicle the same day
You may fetch a different vehicle and continue immediately
The examination continues regardless, with points deducted
You must return in seven days regardless of the defect
questions.explanation: The examiner may allow a minor defect to be corrected so the examination can continue, but the handbook is explicit that you will not be permitted to continue in another vehicle on the same test date. Switching cars is the option that is closed off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you will not be permitted to continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date

questions.question: Your test is stopped because of a vehicle defect and your friend offers to lend you her car, parked nearby. Why does that not solve the problem?
choices: You may not continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date
Her car would also need a road test of its own
Only a vehicle owned by the applicant may be used
The examiner would need written permission from the owner
questions.explanation: The rule closes the same-day switch: you cannot continue the examination in another vehicle on that test date. Bringing a compliant vehicle in the first place is the only way around it, since the vehicle check happens before you drive.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you will not be permitted to continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date

questions.question: What does the handbook require you to know about the vehicle's safety equipment?
choices: Its location and function, including the parking/emergency brake — being unable to locate and demonstrate any of it is an automatic failure
Only the location of the seat belts and mirrors
Only how to operate the headlights and wipers
Nothing, as the examiner points each item out
questions.explanation: You must know the location and function of all safety equipment, the parking/emergency brake included, and being unable to both locate and demonstrate any of it is an automatic failure on the road skills test. Knowing where it is without being able to use it is not enough.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The applicant must know the location and function of all safety equipment, including the parking/emergency brake.  If the applicant is unable to both locate and demonstrate the use of any of the vehicle safety equipment, this will result in an automatic failure on the road skills test.

questions.question: Which statement about vehicle safety equipment on test day is NOT correct?
choices: Knowing where an item is located is sufficient, even if you cannot operate it
You must know the location and function of all safety equipment
The parking/emergency brake is specifically named
Being unable to locate and demonstrate any item is an automatic failure
questions.explanation: The handbook requires you to both locate and demonstrate the use of the equipment, so pointing at a control you cannot work does not satisfy it. That is why practising in the exact vehicle you will test in matters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The applicant must know the location and function of all safety equipment, including the parking/emergency brake.  If the applicant is unable to both locate and demonstrate the use of any of the vehicle safety equipment, this will result in an automatic failure on the road skills test.

questions.question: At what point does window tint become illegal equipment?
choices: When windows are tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission
When windows are tinted at all
When windows are tinted to less than 70 percent light transmission
Only when the windshield itself is tinted
questions.explanation: The illegal equipment list names windows tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission. Because tint is checked as part of the vehicle check, it can stop a road test before it starts.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Windows tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission

questions.question: You have aftermarket tint on your side windows and plan to use the car for your road test. Why is that worth checking first?
choices: Tint below 35 percent light transmission is illegal equipment, and vehicle defects may constitute failure of examination
Tint is only an issue for night-time road tests
Tint is permitted on side windows but not the rear window
Tint has no bearing on the road test
questions.explanation: Window tint under 35 percent light transmission appears on the illegal equipment list, and the examiner checks the vehicle against the equipment laws before the test. The handbook also says the examiner cannot give the driving test unless the vehicle is legally equipped.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Windows tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission

questions.question: Why are red and/or blue flashing lights on the illegal equipment list?
choices: Only authorized emergency vehicles may have those warning lights
They draw too much power from the vehicle's battery
They are permitted only on vehicles over a certain weight
They are legal but must be covered when not in use
questions.explanation: The handbook explains the entry itself: only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights. Sirens, bells and whistles are listed alongside them for the same reason — they imitate an emergency vehicle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Red and/or blue flashing lights (Only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights)

questions.question: Which of these is NOT on the handbook's illegal equipment list?
choices: A single working spotlight
Sirens, bells, or whistles
A cutout or loud-sounding muffler
A broken or cracked windshield
questions.explanation: The list bars more than one spotlight, so a single spotlight is not itself prohibited. Sirens and bells, loud mufflers and a broken or cracked windshield are all named, and any of them can stop the road test at the vehicle check.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Red and/or blue flashing lights (Only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights)

questions.question: When is the road test given?
choices: Only after you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination
On the same visit as the knowledge test, before it is marked
Before the knowledge examination, to save a second trip
Only after a second vision screening
questions.explanation: The road test is not given until you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination. That ordering, plus the minimum permit-holding period from Chapter I, sets how quickly anyone can reach a licence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The road test, or driving examination, will not be given until you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination.

questions.question: An applicant asks to take the road test first because they are a confident driver but a nervous test-taker. What does the handbook allow?
choices: Nothing — the road test is not given until the knowledge examination has been passed
The order may be reversed at the examiner's discretion
Both may be taken on the same day in either order
The knowledge test may be waived for an experienced driver
questions.explanation: The sequence is fixed: the road test follows the knowledge examination. Confidence behind the wheel does not substitute for the knowledge the written test measures, which is drawn entirely from this handbook.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The road test, or driving examination, will not be given until you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination.

questions.question: What does the handbook tell you to do before driving away on the test?
choices: Adjust the vehicle seat and rear view mirror, because proper seat adjustment assures better control
Test the horn and the hazard lights
Drive a lap of the car park to warm up
Ask the examiner to confirm the route in advance
questions.explanation: Adjusting the seat and rear view mirror before driving is stated directly, and the handbook explains why: proper seat adjustment assures better control of the vehicle, and a correct mirror helps you see behind when slowing, changing lanes or turning.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Adjust the vehicle seat and rear view mirror before driving.  Proper seat  adjustment assures better control of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which habit does the handbook specifically warn against during the driving examination?
choices: Resting your elbow in the window instead of keeping both hands on the wheel
Checking your mirrors too frequently
Signalling earlier than necessary
Braking gently on approach to a stop
questions.explanation: The handbook says to keep both hands on the steering wheel and not to rest your elbow in the window. Elsewhere it adds that all steering methods are acceptable provided both hands stay on the outside of the wheel, with no palming.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Adjust the vehicle seat and rear view mirror before driving.  Proper seat  adjustment assures better control of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which exercises may form part of the basic control skills test?
choices: Left and right side parallel parking, forward and reverse two-point turnabouts, and a three-point turnabout
Hill starts, emergency braking and skid recovery
Highway merging and lane changes at speed
Reversing around a corner and an emergency stop only
questions.explanation: The handbook lists five exercises and says you may be tested on a subset of them: left side parallel park, right side parallel park, forward two-point turnabout, reverse two-point turnabout, and three-point turnabout. It also advises practising them with a licensed adult over 21 in a safe place.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: During the test, you may be tested on a subset of the following Basic Control Skills exercises:

questions.question: How should you prepare for the basic control skills exercises, according to the handbook?
choices: Practise them with a properly licensed person over 21 in a safe place until you can complete them correctly
Practise them alone on quiet public roads at night
Wait for the examiner to demonstrate each one on test day
Practise only parallel parking, since the others are optional
questions.explanation: The handbook recommends practising with a parent, guardian or friend who is properly licensed and over 21, in a safe place such as a parking lot or residential area, and in a variety of vehicles and locations. You may be tested on any subset of the exercises, so none of them is safe to skip.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: During the test, you may be tested on a subset of the following Basic Control Skills exercises:

questions.question: How are turn signal mistakes scored during the exercises?
choices: Each failure to use or improper use of the signal counts as an error
Only the first missed signal is counted
Signal errors are noted but do not affect the score
Signal errors count only during lane changes
questions.explanation: Every instance counts: each time you fail to use or improperly use your turn signal it is an error. The handbook adds that if your signal cancels automatically you must reactivate it when necessary, so a cancelled signal mid-manoeuvre is your responsibility.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: Each time you fail to use or improperly use your turn signal it will count as an error.

questions.question: During an exercise your signal cancels itself partway through the manoeuvre and you do not switch it back on. How is that treated?
choices: As an error, because a signal that cancels automatically must be reactivated when necessary
As acceptable, because the signal was used at the start
As acceptable, because automatic cancellation is a vehicle function
As an automatic failure of the road test
questions.explanation: The handbook expressly puts the burden on the driver to reactivate a signal that cancels automatically. It counts as a signal error rather than an automatic failure — but signal errors accumulate, and excessive points during the road test is itself disqualifying.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: Each time you fail to use or improperly use your turn signal it will count as an error.

questions.question: How far back should you stop behind another vehicle?
choices: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
One full car length, measured by eye
Close enough that your bumper nearly touches theirs
Three car lengths in all conditions
questions.explanation: The handbook gives a practical reference rather than a distance: stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead. It works at any vehicle height and leaves room to pull around if the car in front cannot move.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A safe gap when stopping behind another vehicle is to stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: You stop behind a car at a red light and can see only the top of its rear bumper. What does the handbook's reference tell you?
choices: You are too close — you should be able to see the vehicle's rear tires
You are correctly positioned for a traffic light
You are too far back and should close the gap
The reference applies only at stop signs
questions.explanation: Being unable to see the rear tires means the gap is smaller than the handbook's safe-gap reference. The same guidance appears for stopping behind a vehicle at intersections and before turns, so it is not limited to one kind of stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A safe gap when stopping behind another vehicle is to stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: What should you expect regarding traffic signs during the road test?
choices: To be asked to identify a number of signs, which can be located anywhere on the route
To be shown printed sign cards at the end of the test
To be asked about signs only if you make a driving error
Nothing — signs are covered only in the knowledge test
questions.explanation: During the road test you will be asked to identify a number of traffic signs, and they can be anywhere on the route. The handbook adds that if the examiner asks what sign you just passed, you should be able to tell them — which means noticing signs as you drive, not just recognising them on a card.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: During the road test you will be asked to identify a number of traffic signs.  They can be located anywhere on the road test.

questions.question: The examiner asks what the sign you just passed meant, and you did not notice it. What does this tell you about how to drive the test?
choices: Signs must be actively read as you drive, because you may be asked about any sign on the route
Only signs at intersections are examinable
The examiner will always point out a sign before asking about it
Sign questions are optional and can be declined
questions.explanation: The handbook says the signs can be located anywhere on the road test and that you should be able to tell the examiner about a sign you just passed. That is a scan-and-read habit, not a memorisation exercise, and it is the same habit that keeps a licensed driver safe.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: During the road test you will be asked to identify a number of traffic signs.  They can be located anywhere on the road test.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as an automatic failure?
choices: Hitting, tapping or moving a cone, barrel or flag
Stalling the engine once during the test
Signalling later than the examiner expected
Braking more firmly than necessary at a stop sign
questions.explanation: The automatic failures list names hitting, tapping or moving a cone, barrel or flag, along with jumping a curb and accumulating excessive points. Touching a marker at all is enough — the handbook does not distinguish between a tap and a knock.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Hitting, tapping, or moving a cone, barrel, or flag

questions.question: During a parallel parking exercise your rear tire brushes a cone, which rocks but does not fall. What is the result?
choices: An automatic failure — hitting, tapping or moving a cone is disqualifying
An error scored as points, not a failure
No penalty, since the cone stayed upright
A warning, with the exercise repeated
questions.explanation: The handbook covers hitting, tapping or moving the marker, so a cone that rocks has been moved. Jumping a curb during any part of the driving test is treated the same way, which is why slow, deliberate positioning beats speed in these exercises.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Hitting, tapping, or moving a cone, barrel, or flag

questions.question: What happens if you do not use your safety belt during the road test?
choices: You are disqualified
You lose points but may continue
You are warned once and then disqualified
Nothing, if the examiner is belted
questions.explanation: Not using your safety belt appears on the list of errors that disqualify you from the road test. The road test score form carries it as a separate automatic failure line, so it is checked deliberately rather than incidentally.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you do not use your safety belt

questions.question: Which of these road-test errors is NOT an automatic disqualification?
choices: Stopping slightly further back from the stop line than necessary
Not using your safety belt
Using a wireless communications device at any time
Failing to yield to pedestrians or other roadway users
questions.explanation: Stopping a little early is a positioning matter scored as points, whereas belts, devices and failing to yield are all named among the road skills test automatic failures. Knowing which errors are recoverable helps you keep composure when one happens.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you do not use your safety belt

questions.question: When may you use a wireless communications device during the road test?
choices: Never — using it at any time disqualifies you
Only to answer a call from a parent or guardian
Only when the vehicle is stopped
Only hands-free, as with ordinary driving
questions.explanation: The handbook uses the words 'if at anytime you use your wireless communications device' among the disqualifying errors, leaving no exception for hands-free use or for a stopped vehicle. The safest approach is to leave the phone switched off and out of reach.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If at anytime you use your wireless communications device

questions.question: Your phone rings during the road test and you decline the call with one tap. What is the result?
choices: Disqualification — using the device at any time during the test ends it
Nothing, because you did not answer the call
A points deduction for distraction
Nothing, provided the examiner did not have to intervene
questions.explanation: Declining a call is still using the device, and the disqualification is written to cover any use at any time. Because this is one of the easiest automatic failures to avoid entirely, the phone belongs switched off before the test begins.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If at anytime you use your wireless communications device

questions.question: What does the handbook say if the examiner has to take control of the vehicle?
choices: You are disqualified
The test is paused and resumed
Points are deducted for the incident
The manoeuvre is repeated
questions.explanation: If the examiner has to take control of the vehicle you are disqualified. The same list also disqualifies you for committing an unsafe act or forcing another driver to take evasive action, so the standard is about danger created, not just the intervention itself.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the examiner has to take control of the vehicle

questions.question: Which situation matches the handbook's automatic failure for examiner intervention?
choices: The examiner grabs the wheel as you drift toward an oncoming vehicle
The examiner repeats a direction you did not hear
The examiner points out a sign you missed
The examiner asks you to pull over at the end of the route
questions.explanation: Taking control of the vehicle means physically intervening in the driving, as with grabbing the wheel or the brake. Repeating a direction or asking a question is normal examiner communication, not intervention.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the examiner has to take control of the vehicle

questions.question: A licence requires corrective lenses and the applicant arrives without them. How does the road test treat this?
choices: Failing to wear your glasses if required is a disqualifying error
The test proceeds with a points deduction
The test proceeds if the applicant can read a sign at 20 metres
The applicant is rescheduled without penalty
questions.explanation: The road skills test automatic failures include failing to wear your glasses if required. This connects directly to the vision screening, where needing lenses to reach 20/40 is what puts the restriction on the licence in the first place.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you fail to wear your glasses if required

questions.question: Which statement about required glasses is NOT correct?
choices: An applicant may substitute sunglasses if prescription lenses are forgotten
Failing to wear required glasses disqualifies you on the road test
The requirement arises from the vision screening result
The restriction is recorded as a code on the licence
questions.explanation: Nothing in the handbook permits substituting a different pair of lenses for the prescription the restriction requires. The other statements describe the chain accurately: the screening sets the restriction, the restriction shows as a code, and ignoring it disqualifies you on the road test.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you fail to wear your glasses if required

questions.question: How soon may an applicant who fails the knowledge or road skills test be tested again?
choices: Not twice within a period of one week
The same day, at a different location
After 30 days
After completing a driver improvement course
questions.explanation: The handbook bars testing twice within a period of one week for applicants who fail either the knowledge or road skills test, citing §17B-2-6 of the West Virginia State Code. The bar applies to both tests, not just the road test.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants who fail either the knowledge or road skills test may not be tested twice within a period of one (1) week, in accordance with §17B-2-6, West Virginia State Code.

questions.question: An applicant fails the knowledge test on Monday and tries to retake it at another office on Wednesday. What does the handbook say?
choices: They may not be tested twice within one week, regardless of location
A different office is permitted, since the bar applies per location
They may retake it once the fee is paid again
The bar applies only to the road skills test
questions.explanation: The one-week rule is written about the applicant, not the office, and it covers both the knowledge and the road skills test. Since each knowledge test attempt also carries a $7.50 fee, there is a cost as well as a delay to a rushed second attempt.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants who fail either the knowledge or road skills test may not be tested twice within a period of one (1) week, in accordance with §17B-2-6, West Virginia State Code.

questions.question: What must all first-time applicants complete, and when?
choices: A short DUI awareness course, given upon passing the road skills test
A defensive driving class, before the knowledge test
An alcohol awareness course, before the vision screening
A first aid course, within 30 days of licensing
questions.explanation: The DMV requires all first-time applicants for a driver's license or motorcycle-only licence to complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test. On completing it you receive a card or a stamp on your application showing completion.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The DMV requires that all first-time applicants for a driver's license or motorcycle-only West Virginia driver's license complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test.

questions.question: A driver previously licensed in West Virginia moves back from another state. Does the DUI awareness course apply to them?
choices: Yes — the course must be completed by all out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia, even if previously licensed here
No, because they have held a WV licence before
No, because the course applies only to applicants under 21
Only if their previous WV licence expired more than three years ago
questions.explanation: The handbook says the course must be completed by all out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia even if they have been previously licensed in West Virginia. Having held a WV licence in the past does not exempt anyone.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The DMV requires that all first-time applicants for a driver's license or motorcycle-only West Virginia driver's license complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test.

questions.question: Which lane should slower traffic use on an interstate?
choices: The right-hand lane, except when passing
The left-hand lane, to stay clear of merging traffic
Any lane, as long as the speed limit is not exceeded
The centre lane on a three-lane interstate
questions.explanation: The handbook states that slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane except when passing. It repeats the rule later in the chapter, adding that a slow vehicle in the wrong lane forces other drivers into abrupt lane changes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane, except when passing.

questions.question: You are travelling at the speed limit in the left lane of a two-lane interstate with nothing ahead of you. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: Move back to the right-hand lane, which is where you belong unless passing
Stay in the left lane, since you are already at the limit
Stay in the left lane to keep the right lane clear for merging traffic
Move right only if a faster vehicle appears behind you
questions.explanation: The left lane is for passing, and the handbook's instruction is to drive in the right-hand lane except when passing. Being at the limit does not make the left lane yours, and it is the lane discipline rather than your speed that keeps traffic flowing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane, except when passing.

questions.question: What does the handbook ask of you when trucks and buses are entering an interstate?
choices: Be cooperative and give them extra time and space to adjust to the traffic flow
Speed up so they can merge behind you
Move to the left lane and maintain your speed exactly
Sound your horn to signal that you have seen them
questions.explanation: The handbook says trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns and asks drivers to be cooperative, giving them extra time and space. Their size and weight mean they cannot change speed the way a car can.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Remember that trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns.

questions.question: A loaded tractor-trailer is on the entrance ramp as you approach in the right lane. Which response fits the handbook's guidance?
choices: Give it extra time and space to adjust to the traffic flow
Hold your exact speed and position so the driver can predict you
Accelerate past the merge point as quickly as possible
Move onto the shoulder to leave the lane clear
questions.explanation: The handbook singles out trucks and buses as needing extra time to adjust to traffic patterns and asks drivers to be cooperative with time and space. Using the shoulder is not an option — shoulders are for disabled vehicles only.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Remember that trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns.

questions.question: Which direction do even-numbered interstates run?
choices: East to west
North to south
Always toward the nearest city
The direction is not indicated by the number
questions.explanation: Even-numbered interstates run east to west, and odd-numbered interstates run north to south. Because the numbering is national, it works as a rough compass anywhere in the country.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Even-numbered interstates run east to west.

questions.question: You join an odd-numbered two-digit interstate. What does the number tell you about its general direction?
choices: It runs north to south
It runs east to west
It is a bypass around a city
It is a spur route into a city
questions.explanation: Odd-numbered interstates run north to south, while even numbers run east to west. Beltways and spurs are indicated by three-digit numbers rather than by odd or even two-digit ones.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Odd-numbered interstates run north to south.

questions.question: What does a three-digit interstate number beginning with an even digit identify?
choices: A beltway or bypass around a city
A spur route into a city
A toll road
A route that crosses a state line
questions.explanation: Three-digit numbers with an even first number identify beltways or bypasses around cities, while an odd first number identifies a spur route. The distinction tells you whether the road will take you around a city or into it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Three-digit numbers with an even first number identify beltways or bypasses around cities.

questions.question: Which statement about interstate numbering is NOT correct?
choices: A three-digit number beginning with an odd digit identifies a beltway around a city
A three-digit number beginning with an even digit identifies a beltway or bypass
Even-numbered interstates run east to west
Odd-numbered interstates run north to south
questions.explanation: It is the even first digit that marks a beltway or bypass; an odd first digit marks a spur route. The other three statements are exactly as the handbook gives them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Three-digit numbers with an even first number identify beltways or bypasses around cities.

questions.question: Why does the handbook tell you to plan an interstate route in advance?
choices: Because interstate entrances and exits are sometimes far apart
Because interstate routes change frequently
Because navigation devices are prohibited on interstates
Because exits are unmarked until you reach them
questions.explanation: The reason given is that entrances and exits are sometimes far apart, which makes a wrong turn expensive in time and distance. The handbook pairs this with checking the vehicle, since a breakdown on an interstate is both costly and dangerous.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Since interstate entrances and exits are sometimes far apart, it is important to plan your route in advance.  Make sure your vehicle is in good working condition.

questions.question: Which preparation does the handbook specifically recommend before an interstate trip?
choices: Checking gas, water, oil and tires, including the spare tire
Filling the tank at the last exit before joining
Carrying a printed map instead of a navigation device
Driving the route once at a quieter time first
questions.explanation: The handbook says to make sure your vehicle is in good working condition and lists gas, water, oil and tires including the spare. Its reasoning is blunt: a breakdown on an interstate can cost a lot of time and can be dangerous.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Since interstate entrances and exits are sometimes far apart, it is important to plan your route in advance.  Make sure your vehicle is in good working condition.

questions.question: Where is the first guide sign for an interchange placed?
choices: Well in advance of the point where you must turn off
At the start of the deceleration lane
At the exit gore itself
Immediately after the previous exit
questions.explanation: The first guide sign is placed well in advance of the turn-off, which the handbook says permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly. It exists so you can avoid hazardous last-minute manoeuvres.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: On interstates, the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well in advance of the point where you must turn off.  This permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly.

questions.question: You see the first guide sign for your exit a long way ahead. What is that distance for?
choices: To give you ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly
To warn that the exit may be closed
To indicate that the exit ramp curves sharply
To mark the beginning of the deceleration lane
questions.explanation: The handbook explains that the advance placement permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly, and tells you to pay attention to the guide signs to avoid hazardous last-minute manoeuvres. A sharp ramp curve is warned by an advisory speed limit sign instead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: On interstates, the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well in advance of the point where you must turn off.  This permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly.

questions.question: Why does the handbook tell you to pay careful attention to the signs at an interstate entrance?
choices: Because an exit ramp is often next to the entrance ramp, marked Do Not Enter and Wrong Way
Because entrance ramps are often unmarked
Because the speed limit changes at every ramp
Because ramps may be closed without notice
questions.explanation: The handbook warns that an exit ramp will often sit next to the entrance ramp, carrying Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs. Reading the signs is what keeps you from entering the interstate against the traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Often, an exit ramp will be next to the entrance ramp, marked with “Do Not Enter” and “Wrong Way” signs.

questions.question: You turn into what you think is an entrance ramp and see a Do Not Enter sign facing you. What has happened?
choices: You are about to enter an exit ramp that sits beside the entrance ramp
The interstate is closed ahead
The ramp is restricted to trucks
The ramp is a spur route rather than a through route
questions.explanation: Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs mark the exit ramp that often sits next to the entrance ramp. Those signs face you precisely because you are approaching from the wrong direction, which is the error the handbook is warning about.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Often, an exit ramp will be next to the entrance ramp, marked with “Do Not Enter” and “Wrong Way” signs.

questions.question: What does an advisory speed limit sign on a ramp indicate?
choices: That the ramp curves sharply
The minimum speed required to merge
The speed limit of the interstate you are joining
That the ramp is under construction
questions.explanation: Advisory speed limit signs are used on ramps that curve sharply. They are a warning about the ramp's geometry, not about the speed you will need once you reach the acceleration lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Look for any advisory speed limit signs on the ramp.  These are used if the ramp curves sharply.

questions.question: An advisory sign on an entrance ramp shows 25 mph. What does it tell you, and what happens next?
choices: The ramp curves sharply, so slow for the curve — you will still need to accelerate to traffic speed before merging
The interstate you are joining has a 25 mph limit
You must merge at 25 mph
You must maintain 25 mph until the end of the acceleration lane
questions.explanation: The advisory speed addresses a sharp ramp curve. Once through it, the handbook's merging steps still apply: find a gap and adjust your speed to meet it so you are travelling the same speed as traffic when you merge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Look for any advisory speed limit signs on the ramp.  These are used if the ramp curves sharply.

questions.question: At what point on the entrance ramp should you begin the merging steps?
choices: About halfway along the ramp
At the very start of the ramp
At the end of the acceleration lane
Once you are level with traffic
questions.explanation: The handbook says that about halfway on the entrance ramp you start taking the steps: checking interstate traffic, signalling, looking for a gap and adjusting your speed to meet it. Starting at that point leaves enough ramp to actually reach traffic speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: About halfway on the entrance ramp, start taking these steps:

questions.question: Which sequence matches the handbook's merging steps?
choices: Check interstate traffic, use your turn signal, look for a gap, adjust your speed to meet it, then merge at the speed of traffic
Stop at the end of the ramp, wait for a gap, then accelerate into it
Signal, move left immediately, then match the speed of traffic
Accelerate to the limit first, then look for a gap as you merge
questions.explanation: The handbook's order is check, signal, find a gap, adjust speed to the gap, then merge travelling at the same speed as other traffic. It also warns not to cut sharply left — follow the lane, merge, and only then change lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: About halfway on the entrance ramp, start taking these steps:

questions.question: How does the handbook tell you to check interstate traffic while on the entrance ramp?
choices: With quick glances over your shoulder and to the side
By relying on your side mirror alone
By turning your head and holding the look until a gap appears
By watching the traffic in your rear view mirror only
questions.explanation: The instruction is quick glances over your shoulder and to the side, while also watching the vehicles ahead of you entering the acceleration lane. Quick is the operative word — a long look away from the ramp ahead is its own hazard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Take quick glances over your shoulder and to the side.

questions.question: Why does the handbook pair shoulder glances with watching the vehicles in front of you on the ramp?
choices: Because a vehicle ahead in the acceleration lane may slow or stop without warning
Because the vehicle ahead will signal the gap you should use
Because you must merge in the same order you entered the ramp
Because the vehicle ahead shows where the acceleration lane ends
questions.explanation: The handbook tells you to be prepared to adjust your driving if the vehicle ahead in the acceleration lane slows or stops without warning. Your attention has to be split between the traffic you are joining and the car immediately in front of you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Take quick glances over your shoulder and to the side.

questions.question: What does the handbook say about stopping on an entrance ramp or acceleration lane?
choices: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane
Stop if you cannot immediately see a gap
Stop only if a vehicle ahead of you has stopped
Stop at the end of the acceleration lane and wait to be let in
questions.explanation: The instruction is plain: do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane. Entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous, which is why the handbook treats stopping as something to avoid rather than a normal part of merging.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane.

questions.question: Traffic looks heavy as you reach the middle of the entrance ramp. Which response follows the handbook?
choices: Keep moving, find a gap, and adjust your speed to meet it
Stop at the end of the acceleration lane until a large gap appears
Stop on the ramp and signal for another driver to let you in
Cut sharply left into the first available space
questions.explanation: Stopping on the ramp or acceleration lane is ruled out, and so is cutting sharply left — the handbook says to follow the lane, merge with traffic, and then change lanes. Matching your speed to a gap is the technique it actually prescribes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane.

questions.question: If no gap in traffic is available by the end of the acceleration lane, what does the handbook allow?
choices: Driving onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stopping, as a last resort
Stopping in the acceleration lane until a gap appears
Reversing back down the ramp
Merging anyway and expecting traffic to make room
questions.explanation: The handbook permits using the shoulder beyond the acceleration lane and stopping, but calls it a last resort because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous. Stopping in the acceleration lane itself is expressly ruled out.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop

questions.question: Why does the handbook treat the shoulder stop as a last resort rather than a normal option?
choices: Because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous
Because the shoulder is reserved for emergency vehicles
Because stopping there always requires a police report
Because the shoulder is too narrow to hold a vehicle
questions.explanation: The reason given is that entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous — you have no speed to work with and must accelerate into live traffic. The shoulder is otherwise reserved for disabled vehicles, which is a separate rule in the same chapter.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way when you are entering an interstate?
choices: Traffic already on the interstate
The merging vehicle, because it has less room
Whichever vehicle reaches the merge point first
Neither — right-of-way is decided by the ramp signs
questions.explanation: Traffic on the interstate has the right-of-way, and the handbook adds that you cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room. Merging safely is the entering driver's responsibility.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

questions.question: A driver assumes the car in the right lane will move over to let them merge. Why is that assumption dangerous?
choices: Because you cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room
Because moving over is illegal for the driver already on the interstate
Because right-of-way at a merge always belongs to the entering vehicle
Because the other driver cannot legally change lanes near a ramp
questions.explanation: The handbook explicitly warns against relying on other drivers to see you or make room. That is why the merging steps focus on what you control — your timing, your gap and your speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

questions.question: When should you signal and move into the lane for your exit?
choices: Well before you have to exit
As you reach the exit gore
Once you are in the deceleration lane
Only if other traffic is present
questions.explanation: The handbook says to signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit, because changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash. The advance guide signs exist to make that possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit.  Changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes for an exit is NOT correct?
choices: A last-moment lane change is acceptable if you signal clearly
Signalling and moving over well before the exit is what the handbook asks
A last-moment change risks missing your exit
A last-moment change risks causing a crash
questions.explanation: Signalling does not cure a late lane change; the handbook names both risks it creates — missing the exit and causing a crash. The remedy it gives is position, not indication.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit.  Changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash.

questions.question: Where should you slow down for an exit?
choices: In the deceleration lane, braking gently to the posted exit ramp limit
On the interstate, well before the exit
On the exit ramp itself, after leaving the deceleration lane
Anywhere, as long as you use your brake lights
questions.explanation: Most exits have a special lane for slowing down, and the handbook says never to slow down on the interstate. Wait until you are in the deceleration lane, then brake gently until your speed matches the posted exit ramp limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Most interstate exits have a special lane for you to slow down in before you reach the exit ramp.  Never slow down on the interstate.

questions.question: A driver begins braking half a mile before the exit while still in the through lane. What is wrong with that?
choices: Never slow down on the interstate — the deceleration lane exists for that
Nothing, provided the brake lights work
Braking early is correct but should be harder
It is only a problem if traffic is following closely
questions.explanation: Slowing in a live lane puts you far below the speed of traffic behind you, which the chapter identifies as creating a hazard and forcing abrupt lane changes. The deceleration lane is provided so speed can be shed out of the traffic stream.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Most interstate exits have a special lane for you to slow down in before you reach the exit ramp.  Never slow down on the interstate.

questions.question: What are interstate shoulders for?
choices: Disabled vehicles only
Short rest stops on long journeys
Changing drivers and checking directions
Any stop of under five minutes
questions.explanation: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles. The handbook names changing drivers and reading a map as things to do in a rest area or after exiting, not on the shoulder.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles.  Do not use the shoulders for changing drivers, reading a map, or other non emergency purposes.

questions.question: You want to swap drivers on a long interstate trip. Where does the handbook say to do it?
choices: In a rest area or after exiting the interstate
On the shoulder, with the four-way flashers on
In the exit gore, which is out of the traffic lane
Anywhere on the shoulder where visibility is good
questions.explanation: Changing drivers is specifically named as a non-emergency use the shoulder is not for; those activities belong in a rest area or after exiting. The gore is worse still — the handbook forbids stopping there because a driver who missed the exit may cross it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles.  Do not use the shoulders for changing drivers, reading a map, or other non emergency purposes.

questions.question: What is an exit gore, and what does the handbook say about it?
choices: The triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp — do not stop in it
