The painted area at the start of the acceleration lane — merge across it
The widened shoulder before an exit — park there only in emergencies
The median crossover — use it only to turn around
questions.explanation: The gore is the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp, and the handbook says not to stop in it because another driver who has missed the exit may try to cross it and strike your vehicle. It is a space drivers cut across, not a refuge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop in an exit gore (the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp).

questions.question: Why is stopping in an exit gore particularly dangerous?
choices: A driver who has missed the exit may cross it and strike your vehicle
It is the narrowest part of the shoulder
Emergency vehicles use it to reach crashes
It is not visible to drivers on the ramp
questions.explanation: The handbook gives exactly this reason: another driver may try to cross the gore after missing the exit. It is the one place on the roadside where a car is most likely to arrive unexpectedly and at speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop in an exit gore (the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp).

questions.question: What does the handbook say about U-turns on an interstate?
choices: Never make one — go to the next exit to turn around
Make one only where a paved median crossover is provided
Make one only when traffic is light and visibility is good
Make one only to reach an exit you have just missed
questions.explanation: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate; go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering. The gravel or paved crossovers in some medians are for police and emergency vehicles only.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate.  Go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering the interstate.

questions.question: You miss your exit and notice a paved crossover in the median a few hundred metres ahead. What does the handbook say?
choices: The crossover is for police and emergency vehicles only — continue to the next exit
Use the crossover, since it is provided for turning around
Use the crossover only if you signal and traffic is clear
Reverse along the shoulder to the exit you missed
questions.explanation: Median crossovers are reserved for police and emergency vehicles, and the handbook tells you never to make a U-turn on an interstate. Going on to the next exit is the answer to a missed exit, as it is to almost every version of this problem.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate.  Go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering the interstate.

questions.question: What minimum speed does the handbook give for interstate driving?
choices: Do not drive slower than 55 mph unless conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted
Do not drive slower than 45 mph under any circumstances
There is no minimum speed on an interstate
Do not drive slower than 65 mph unless conditions are bad
questions.explanation: The handbook says not to drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted. It sits alongside the instruction never to exceed the legal limit, so the rule bounds you from both sides.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted.

questions.question: Heavy rain has reduced visibility on the interstate and you slow to 45 mph. Does that conflict with the minimum speed guidance?
choices: No — the minimum does not apply when weather or road conditions are bad
Yes — 55 mph is required in all circumstances
Yes, unless a variable message sign has lowered the limit
No, because minimum speeds apply only to trucks
questions.explanation: The 55 mph floor carries its own exceptions: bad weather or road conditions, or a posted lower speed. In adverse conditions the handbook actively tells you to adjust speed so a safe stop remains possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted.

questions.question: Why does driving much slower than other traffic create a hazard?
choices: Because other drivers may be forced to change lanes abruptly
Because slow vehicles use more fuel
Because slow driving is always a moving violation
Because brake lights are less visible at low speed
questions.explanation: The handbook explains that crashes may happen because other drivers are forced to change lanes abruptly around a much slower vehicle. This is the same reasoning behind keeping right and shedding speed in the deceleration lane rather than the through lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you drive on interstates at a speed much slower than other  drivers, you create a hazard.

questions.question: Which statement about speed on interstates is NOT supported by the handbook?
choices: Driving well below the flow of traffic is always the safest choice
You should never drive faster than the legal speed limit
Driving much slower than other drivers creates a hazard
You should always drive at a steady speed
questions.explanation: The handbook treats a large speed difference as the hazard, not speed itself, and asks for a steady speed within the limit. Driving well below the flow is the behaviour it warns against, because it forces abrupt lane changes around you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you drive on interstates at a speed much slower than other  drivers, you create a hazard.

questions.question: What does the handbook require during adverse conditions on an interstate?
choices: Headlights must be turned on
Hazard flashers must be turned on
You must leave the interstate at the next exit
You must move to the left lane
questions.explanation: Headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions, in accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code. The handbook pairs that with increasing following distance and adjusting speed so a safe stop is possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code, headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions.

questions.question: Besides turning on headlights, what two adjustments does the handbook call especially important in adverse conditions?
choices: Maintaining adequate following distance and adjusting speed to allow a safe stop
Using hazard flashers and moving to the right lane
Increasing speed to clear the affected area quickly
Turning on the high beams and sounding the horn
questions.explanation: The handbook says it is especially important to maintain an adequate following distance and adjust your speed to ensure the possibility of a safe stop. Both are about preserving the room and time you need when traction and visibility are reduced.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code, headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle becomes disabled on an interstate?
choices: Move as far off the road as possible, turn on the four-way flashers, and get everyone out and well away from the road
Stay in the vehicle with the doors locked and wait for help
Stop in the exit gore where you are more visible
Leave the vehicle in the right lane with the hazard lights on
questions.explanation: The handbook gives three actions together: get as far off the road as possible, put on the four-way flashers, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road. Staying inside a car on the shoulder is what it specifically does not tell you to do.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle  becomes disabled, move as far off the road as possible, turn on your four-way flashers to indicate your vehicle is stopped, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road.

questions.question: Your engine dies and you coast onto the shoulder. Passengers want to stay in the car because it is cold. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: Everyone should get out of the vehicle and move well away from the road
Passengers may stay inside if seat belts remain fastened
Passengers should stay inside so the vehicle is easier to see
Only the driver should leave the vehicle to set out flares
questions.explanation: The instruction is to get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road. The chapter also tells drivers to be particularly alert for stopped vehicles, which is the reason a car on the shoulder is not a safe place to sit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle  becomes disabled, move as far off the road as possible, turn on your four-way flashers to indicate your vehicle is stopped, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road.

questions.question: Where should flares be placed for a disabled vehicle?
choices: One about a vehicle length behind and another about 300 feet back
Both directly behind the vehicle's rear bumper
One 50 feet ahead and one 50 feet behind
One in the through lane to close it off
questions.explanation: The handbook specifies one flare about one vehicle length behind the vehicle and another about 300 feet back, each placed on the shoulder near the edge of the through lane. The far flare gives approaching drivers warning at interstate speeds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Put a flare about one (1) vehicle length behind your vehicle and another about 300 feet back.

questions.question: Why does the second flare go about 300 feet back rather than close to the vehicle?
choices: So drivers approaching at interstate speed get warning well before they reach you
So the flare is visible from the opposite carriageway
So it marks the edge of the shoulder for tow operators
So it does not set fire to the disabled vehicle
questions.explanation: At interstate speeds a warning placed close to the vehicle arrives too late to be useful, so the distant flare buys approaching drivers time to react. Both flares go on the shoulder near the edge of the through lane, where they can be seen by traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Put a flare about one (1) vehicle length behind your vehicle and another about 300 feet back.

questions.question: What does the handbook suggest in very dense fog?
choices: It may be better to leave the interstate and use slower roads to reach your destination
Use high beams to see further through the fog
Follow the vehicle ahead closely to keep its lights in view
Stop on the shoulder until the fog clears
questions.explanation: The handbook says that if fog is very dense it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads. Stopping on the shoulder is not the answer — shoulders are for disabled vehicles, and the chapter warns drivers to be alert for stopped vehicles as a hazard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the fog is very dense, it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads to reach your destination.

questions.question: You are involved in a crash on an interstate in heavy fog. What does the handbook tell you to try to do?
choices: Get your vehicle off the road as far as possible, because leaving it on the road invites further crashes
Leave the vehicle exactly where it stopped until police arrive
Move the vehicle to the exit gore
Drive on to the next exit before stopping
questions.explanation: The handbook says to try to get the vehicle off the road as far as possible, and warns that leaving it on the road until police arrive invites further crashes. In dense fog, a stationary vehicle in a live lane is close to invisible until it is too late.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the fog is very dense, it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads to reach your destination.

questions.question: What should you do when signs warn that a lane is closed ahead?
choices: Move over to the open lane as soon as possible
Stay in the closing lane until the merge point to keep traffic even
Slow to 20 mph immediately
